MailClaw exposes a local inbound webhook endpoint you can POST contact and event data to. When your cart abandonment event fires, send a payload like this:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/inbound/webhook \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "alex@example.com",
    "first_name": "Alex",
    "cart_value": 89.95,
    "cart_url": "https://yourstore.com/cart/recover?token=abc123",
    "trigger": "cart_abandoned",
    "sequence": "abandoned-cart-v1"
  }'

The trigger field maps directly to a sequence entry point you'll define in the next step. The sequence field tells MailClaw which flow to enroll this contact in. Once the webhook receives this payload, the contact is created (or updated if they already exist) and enrollment begins automatically.

Using the MailClaw CLI

If you're testing locally or want to manually seed contacts, the CLI is your fastest path:

# Enroll a single contact into a sequence
mailclaw sequence enroll --email alex@example.com --sequence abandoned-cart-v1

# Import a CSV of lapsed cart contacts
mailclaw contacts import --file abandoned_july.csv --sequence abandoned-cart-v1

Building the Sequence in the Dashboard

Open the MailClaw dashboard at http://localhost:3100 and navigate to Sequences → New Sequence. Name it something memorable like abandoned-cart-v1 — you'll reference this slug in your webhook payloads.

The Three-Email Structure That Works

Abandoned cart sequences perform best with three touches spaced strategically. Here's the framework:

  1. Email 1 — The Gentle Reminder (1 hour after abandonment): No pressure. Just a friendly nudge that their cart is saved. Include the cart URL and a single clear call to action.
  2. Email 2 — Social Proof + Urgency (24 hours after abandonment): Add a review or testimonial about the product they left behind. Mention limited stock if it's true. Never manufacture fake urgency — it destroys trust and hurts deliverability.
  3. Email 3 — The Offer (48–72 hours after abandonment): If they still haven't converted, offer something: free shipping, a 10% discount, or a bonus. This is your last shot, so make it count.

In the sequence builder, set each step's delay using the Wait block. You can configure delays in minutes, hours, or days. Set conditions on each step — for example, stop the sequence if the contact clicks the cart URL or makes a purchase (more on this below).

Adding Exit Conditions

Nothing damages your sender reputation faster than emailing someone who already bought. In the sequence builder, add a Goal Event block and set it to exit the contact when the purchase_completed trigger fires. Your store should POST this event to the same webhook endpoint:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/inbound/webhook \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "alex@example.com",
    "trigger": "purchase_completed"
  }'

MailClaw will immediately unenroll the contact from all active steps in the sequence.

Writing Better Emails with AI Email Agents

This is where MailClaw's OpenClaw-powered AI email agents genuinely earn their keep. Instead of staring at a blank subject line field, open the AI Agent panel from any email step and describe what you want:

"Write a friendly abandoned cart reminder for a premium skincare brand. The customer left a $90 moisturizer in their cart. Tone should be warm, not pushy. Include a personalization token for first name and a dynamic cart link."

The agent will generate subject line variants, preview text, and body copy with your personalization tokens already inserted. You can iterate in plain English — "make the subject line more curiosity-driven" or "shorten the body to under 100 words" — without ever touching a prompt template manually.

Personalizing with Contact Enrichment

MailClaw's built-in contact enrichment layer can pull additional data points — company, LinkedIn profile, purchase history — to make your emails feel less automated. For B2B stores or high-ticket items, enriched data lets you write copy like:

"Hi Alex, as someone running a design studio, you probably know how much the details matter — which is why we think you'll love the [product] still waiting in your cart."

Enable enrichment on your sequence by toggling Enrich on Enrollment in the sequence settings. MailClaw will attempt to fill in missing fields before Email 1 sends, giving the AI agent more context to work with.

Deliverability: Don't Let Good Emails Land in Spam

Abandoned cart emails are transactional-adjacent, which means they tend to get decent inbox placement — unless you make avoidable mistakes. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring tools surface issues before they become problems.

Pre-Send Checks

Before activating your sequence, run the built-in deliverability audit from the CLI:

mailclaw deliverability check --sequence abandoned-cart-v1

This checks your sending domain's SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, flags any spam-trigger words in your subject lines, and scores your email content. Address any critical warnings before going live — advisory warnings can often be ignored depending on your audience.

Multi-Account Rotation

If you're sending at volume, MailClaw's multi-account support lets you rotate sends across multiple Gmail or Outlook accounts (or a mix of OAuth and SMTP providers like SendGrid). Configure your account pool under Settings → Sending Accounts and assign a rotation strategy to your sequence — round-robin or load-balanced based on daily send limits.

Integrating with Your CRM

If your team lives in HubSpot or Salesforce, you'll want cart recovery activity to sync back. MailClaw supports outbound webhooks on sequence events — when a contact opens, clicks, or converts, you can fire a payload to your CRM's API:

# In sequence settings → Outbound Webhooks
# Event: contact.converted
# Target: https://api.hubspot.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts

mailclaw webhook add \
  --sequence abandoned-cart-v1 \
  --event contact.converted \
  --url https://your-crm-endpoint.com/inbound \
  --method POST

This keeps your sales team informed without requiring them to log into yet another tool. The contact's enriched data and sequence activity travels with the payload.

Measuring What Matters

Pull up the sequence analytics panel in the MailClaw dashboard to track the metrics that actually matter for cart recovery:

  • Recovery rate — percentage of enrolled contacts who completed a purchase
  • Email-level click-to-open rate (CTOR) — tells you whether your copy is resonating once someone opens
  • Sequence exit reasons — how many people converted vs. unsubscribed vs. finished without action
  • Revenue per email — if you're passing cart value through the webhook, MailClaw calculates this automatically

Run the CLI report for a quick snapshot without opening the dashboard:

mailclaw sequence report --sequence abandoned-cart-v1 --range 30d

Putting It All Together

Abandoned cart flows aren't complicated in concept, but most implementations fall apart in the details — stale contact data, emails that fire after someone already bought, subject lines that trigger spam filters. MailClaw handles each of these failure points at the infrastructure level, so you can focus on the copy and strategy that actually moves the needle.

Because everything runs locally and the codebase is open source, you're never locked into a vendor's pricing model or API rate limits. Fork it, extend it, and build the exact recovery flow your store needs — from a single command on your Mac.

articles.title: MailClaw AI Agent: Writing Email Sequences from a Single Prompt
articles.author: Ahmad Saroya
articles.summary: Learn how MailClaw's AI email agent can generate complete, personalized email sequences from a single prompt — including real CLI commands, sequence configuration tips, and best practices for deliverability and contact enrichment.
articles.content:
From One Prompt to a Full Campaign

Most email automation tools make you do the hard work upfront. You stare at a blank sequence builder, wrestle with subject line ideas, agonize over follow-up timing, and end up with something generic that reads like it was written by committee. MailClaw takes a different approach.

The MailClaw AI agent — powered by OpenClaw under the hood — lets you describe what you want in plain language and generates a complete, ready-to-send email sequence in seconds. Not a template. Not a starting point. A real sequence with personalized copy, smart timing, and deliverability-conscious formatting, all from your local machine at localhost:3100.

This article walks you through exactly how that works, from your first prompt to a live campaign.

How the MailClaw AI Agent Actually Works

The AI agent in MailClaw isn't a simple autocomplete wrapper. It operates as a multi-step reasoning system that understands campaign intent, audience context, and email best practices simultaneously. When you submit a prompt, the agent:

  • Identifies the campaign goal (cold outreach, nurture, re-engagement, onboarding, etc.)
  • Determines the optimal sequence length and email cadence based on the goal
  • Writes subject lines, preview text, and body copy for each step
  • Injects personalization tokens for contact-level data (name, company, role, etc.)
  • Flags any copy that could trigger spam filters using MailClaw's built-in deliverability analyzer

All of this runs locally. No data leaves your machine. No API rate-limit surprises mid-campaign. It's one of the reasons MailClaw's open-source model resonates with developers and growth teams who want control without sacrificing capability.

Writing Your First Sequence Prompt

The quality of what the agent produces scales directly with the quality of your prompt. Vague input produces generic output. Specific input produces sequences that feel handcrafted.

A Weak Prompt vs. a Strong Prompt

Here's the difference in practice:

Weak: "Write a cold email sequence for a SaaS product."
Strong: "Write a 4-step cold outreach sequence targeting VP-level engineering leaders at Series B startups. We're selling a developer observability platform. Pain points: alert fatigue, slow incident response, too many siloed monitoring tools. Tone: direct, peer-to-peer, no fluff. Goal: book a 20-minute demo call."

The second prompt gives the agent everything it needs — audience, product, pain points, tone, and conversion goal. You'll get copy that sounds like it was written by someone who actually knows the space.

Running the Prompt via CLI

MailClaw's command-line interface is the fastest way to kick off a sequence generation. With your local server running, open a terminal and use the mclaw agent generate command:

mclaw agent generate \
  --goal "cold-outreach" \
  --steps 4 \
  --audience "VP Engineering at Series B startups" \
  --product "developer observability platform" \
  --pain-points "alert fatigue, slow MTTR, tool sprawl" \
  --tone "direct, peer-to-peer" \
  --cta "book a 20-minute demo" \
  --output sequences/vp-eng-outreach.json

The agent writes the full sequence to a JSON file, which you can immediately import into the MailClaw sequence builder, review in the local dashboard, or edit before sending. You never have to touch the dashboard if you prefer to stay in the terminal — but the dashboard at localhost:3100 makes reviewing and tweaking copy significantly easier.

Reviewing the Output in the Sequence Builder

Once the file is generated, import it directly into the visual sequence builder:

mclaw sequence import sequences/vp-eng-outreach.json --name "VP Eng Cold Outreach Q3"

Open localhost:3100 in your browser and navigate to Sequences. You'll see all four emails laid out with timing gaps the agent has already reasoned about — typically Day 1, Day 3, Day 7, and Day 14 for a cold outreach goal, adjusted slightly based on the audience type and product complexity.

What to Look For When Reviewing

The AI gets about 85% of the way there on a strong prompt. Here's where human review adds the most value:

  • Step 1 subject line: Make sure it doesn't read as clickbait. The deliverability panel in MailClaw will score it automatically — aim for green.
  • Personalization tokens: The agent inserts tokens like {{first_name}}, {{company}}, and {{job_title}}. Verify these map to the fields in your contact list, especially if you're pulling contacts from HubSpot or Salesforce via MailClaw's CRM sync.
  • Step 3 and 4 tone: Late-sequence emails often need to be softer or more direct depending on whether prior emails got opens. Consider branching here if your campaign warrants it.
  • CTA clarity: The agent tends to embed the CTA naturally in the body. If your conversion path is a calendar link, make sure it's clearly visible and not buried in a paragraph.

Enriching Contacts Before You Send

A great sequence is still dead weight without accurate contact data. MailClaw's contact enrichment feature runs before your first send and fills in the gaps — job title, company size, LinkedIn URL, industry, tech stack signals — so your personalization tokens actually resolve to something meaningful.

mclaw contacts enrich --list lists/vp-eng-targets.csv --provider clearbit

You can also chain enrichment directly into the agent workflow, so by the time your sequence is generated, the contact list is already enriched and the agent can use that data to make copy decisions — for example, writing slightly different Step 1 copy for contacts at companies with 50 employees versus 500.

Connecting Your Sending Infrastructure

MailClaw supports SMTP and OAuth sending out of the box. Whether you're routing through Gmail, Outlook, SendGrid, or a dedicated cold outreach domain, setup takes under two minutes:

mclaw accounts add \
  --type smtp \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --user apikey \
  --password YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY \
  --alias "Outreach - SendGrid"

For Gmail and Outlook, OAuth is cleaner and avoids app password headaches:

mclaw accounts add --type oauth --provider gmail

This opens a browser flow and stores the token locally. Multi-account support means you can rotate sending across multiple inboxes for higher-volume campaigns without manual management.

Deliverability: Letting the Agent Help You Not Land in Spam

Writing great copy is half the battle. The other half is making sure it arrives. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring runs a pre-send analysis on every sequence, checking for:

  • Spam trigger words and phrase patterns
  • Excessive link density
  • Missing or misconfigured SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records on your sending domain
  • Sending volume ramp recommendations for new domains
  • HTML-to-text ratio issues that affect rendering across clients

You can run this manually at any time:

mclaw sequence check-deliverability --name "VP Eng Cold Outreach Q3"

The output is a scored report with actionable fixes. The AI agent can also auto-revise flagged emails based on the report — run --auto-fix to let it rewrite problematic sections while preserving your original intent.

Launching and Monitoring the Campaign

Once the sequence is reviewed, contacts are enriched, and deliverability checks are green, launching is a single command:

mclaw campaign launch \
  --sequence "VP Eng Cold Outreach Q3" \
  --list lists/vp-eng-targets-enriched.csv \
  --account "Outreach - SendGrid" \
  --start-date 2025-08-01

From the dashboard at localhost:3100/campaigns, you get a live view of open rates, click rates, reply rates, and bounce events as they come in. If a contact replies, MailClaw automatically pauses their sequence — no awkward follow-up emails after someone's already responded.

Iterating with the Agent Mid-Campaign

One of the more powerful patterns is using the agent to revise underperforming steps mid-campaign. If Step 2 is getting low open rates, run:

mclaw agent revise \
  --sequence "VP Eng Cold Outreach Q3" \
  --step 2 \
  --goal "improve open rate" \
  --context "Step 1 open rate is 34%, Step 2 is 11%"

The agent analyzes the existing copy, considers the performance gap, and suggests a revised subject line and preview text. You approve, it updates, and the revision applies to contacts who haven't yet received Step 2.

The Bigger Picture: Agents, Not Just Automation

The shift from traditional email automation to AI agent-driven workflows isn't about replacing human judgment — it's about eliminating the parts of campaign building that are purely mechanical. The parts that make you procrastinate. The parts that used to require a copywriter, a data analyst, and a deliverability consultant working in parallel.

MailClaw brings that into a single open-source tool that runs on your laptop. You stay in control of the strategy and the approval. The agent handles the execution scaffolding.

Start with a strong prompt. Review what comes back. Ship faster than you thought possible.

articles.title: How to Create Seasonal Campaign Templates in MailClaw
articles.author: Sarah Kim
articles.summary: Learn how to build reusable, high-converting seasonal email campaign templates in MailClaw — from Black Friday sequences to holiday drip campaigns — using AI agents, the sequence builder, and smart contact segmentation.
articles.content:
Why Seasonal Templates Are Worth Building Once and Reusing Forever

Every year, the same calendar landmarks roll around — Black Friday, end-of-year sales, New Year promos, Valentine's Day, summer clearance — and most teams scramble to rebuild their email campaigns from scratch each time. That's an enormous waste of energy when the core structure of a seasonal campaign rarely changes dramatically from year to year.

MailClaw's sequence builder and AI email agents make it straightforward to create a library of seasonal templates you can clone, adjust, and deploy in minutes. Once you've done the hard work of crafting the structure, the tone, and the timing logic, future campaigns become a matter of refreshing the copy and updating the dates. This guide walks you through exactly how to do that.

Understanding the Anatomy of a Seasonal Campaign

Before you open the MailClaw dashboard at localhost:3100, it's worth mapping out what a seasonal campaign actually needs. Most high-performing seasonal sequences share the same skeleton:

  • A teaser email — sent 5–7 days before the event, building anticipation
  • A launch email — sent on day one of the campaign with the core offer
  • A reminder email — sent mid-campaign, often with social proof or urgency
  • A last-chance email — sent 24 hours before the deadline
  • A post-campaign follow-up — a thank-you or extended offer for non-converters

This five-email structure works for almost any seasonal event. What changes is the tone, imagery references, subject line hooks, and offer details. Everything else — including your delay logic, branching conditions, and segmentation rules — can be templated and reused.

Setting Up Your First Seasonal Template in MailClaw

Step 1: Create a New Sequence in the Sequence Builder

Navigate to your local MailClaw dashboard at localhost:3100 and head to the Sequences tab. Click New Sequence and give it a descriptive, reusable name like seasonal-blackfriday-base or seasonal-holiday-ecommerce. Naming conventions matter here — you'll be cloning these later, so clarity upfront saves confusion.

If you prefer working from the CLI, MailClaw (built on OpenClaw) lets you scaffold a sequence directly:

openclaw sequence create \
  --name "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --description "5-step Black Friday template" \
  --tags seasonal,blackfriday,template \
  --draft true

The --draft true flag keeps it inactive until you're ready to deploy. This is important when you're building a template — you don't want it to fire prematurely.

Step 2: Add Your Email Steps with Placeholder Variables

The secret to a reusable template is aggressive use of variables. Instead of hardcoding your offer details, use MailClaw's double-brace syntax to inject dynamic values at send time:

Subject: {{campaign.name}} is here — {{offer.discount}} off ends {{offer.deadline}}

Hi {{contact.first_name}},

We've been working on something special for {{campaign.name}}, 
and we wanted you to be the first to know.

{{offer.headline}}

{{offer.body_copy}}

Use code {{offer.promo_code}} at checkout. Valid through {{offer.deadline}}.

— {{sender.name}}

These variables get resolved at the campaign level, so when you clone seasonal-blackfriday-base next November, you just update the campaign variables and every email in the sequence updates automatically. No hunting through five separate email bodies to change a date.

Step 3: Configure Delay Logic and Branching

In the sequence builder, set your delays relative to a campaign start date rather than absolute timestamps. MailClaw supports offset scheduling, which is exactly what you want for templates:

openclaw sequence add-step \
  --sequence "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --step-name "teaser" \
  --delay "-5d" \
  --relative-to "campaign.start_date"

openclaw sequence add-step \
  --sequence "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --step-name "launch" \
  --delay "0d" \
  --relative-to "campaign.start_date"

openclaw sequence add-step \
  --sequence "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --step-name "last-chance" \
  --delay "-1d" \
  --relative-to "campaign.end_date"

Using relative offsets means cloning this template for any future campaign is just a matter of setting a new campaign.start_date and campaign.end_date. The entire timing structure follows automatically.

Using AI Email Agents to Generate Seasonal Variations

Here's where MailClaw's AI email agents really earn their keep. Once you have your base template structure locked in, you can use an agent to generate fresh copy variations tailored to different audience segments or different seasonal events — without rewriting everything yourself.

Generating Copy Variations by Segment

Say your contact list includes both B2B buyers and individual consumers. Your Black Friday messaging for each group should feel meaningfully different. In the MailClaw dashboard under AI Agents, configure a seasonal copy agent like this:

openclaw agent run email-copywriter \
  --template "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --segment "b2b-decision-makers" \
  --tone "professional, ROI-focused" \
  --event "Black Friday" \
  --output-sequence "seasonal-blackfriday-b2b"

The agent reads your base template, understands the structure, and rewrites the body copy and subject lines for the specified segment and tone. You still review and approve before anything goes live — the AI is a first-draft accelerator, not an autopilot.

Adapting Templates Across Seasonal Events

You can also use the AI agent to adapt a Black Friday template into a holiday or New Year campaign. The structural bones stay the same; the agent rewrites the emotional framing and offer language:

openclaw agent run email-copywriter \
  --template "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --event "New Year Sale" \
  --tone "optimistic, fresh-start" \
  --output-sequence "seasonal-newyear-base"

Over time, you'll build a library of seasonal sequences — all sharing the same robust timing and variable architecture, just dressed differently for each occasion.

Enriching Contacts Before Seasonal Campaigns Launch

Segmentation is only as good as your data. Before you fire off a holiday campaign to your entire list, use MailClaw's built-in contact enrichment to fill gaps and sharpen your targeting. Enrichment pulls in firmographic and demographic data that helps you route contacts into the right segment and personalize more deeply.

openclaw contacts enrich \
  --list "holiday-campaign-2024" \
  --fields "company_size,industry,location,job_title" \
  --provider clearbit

MailClaw integrates natively with enrichment providers and can also sync enriched data back to your CRM — whether that's HubSpot, Salesforce, or a CSV-based workflow. Once your contacts are enriched, you can create dynamic segments directly in the dashboard that feed into the right seasonal sequence automatically.

Pro tip: Run contact enrichment at least 48 hours before campaign launch. Enrichment jobs can take time to complete at scale, and you want clean, resolved data driving your segmentation logic — not a half-enriched list.

Connecting to Gmail, Outlook, and SendGrid for Delivery

MailClaw supports both SMTP and OAuth-based sending, which means your seasonal campaigns can go out through whatever sending infrastructure you already use. For high-volume seasonal sends, SendGrid or Amazon SES are solid choices. For smaller, relationship-focused sequences, sending directly through Gmail or Outlook via OAuth often gets better deliverability because the messages originate from a real inbox rather than a transactional IP.

Configure your sending account from the dashboard under Settings → Accounts, or via CLI:

openclaw account add \
  --type oauth \
  --provider gmail \
  --alias "outreach-main"

openclaw account add \
  --type smtp \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --alias "bulk-seasonal"

You can then assign different sending accounts to different sequences — using your personal Gmail OAuth connection for warm prospect sequences, and your SendGrid SMTP for larger broadcast campaigns.

Monitoring Deliverability During Seasonal Peaks

Seasonal campaigns are high-stakes sends. Your entire list is often active at the same time, inbox competition is fierce, and a deliverability dip can quietly kill your results without you noticing until it's too late.

MailClaw's deliverability monitoring dashboard (available at localhost:3100/deliverability) gives you real-time visibility into bounce rates, spam complaint rates, open rates by domain, and inbox placement estimates. Keep a close eye on:

  • Bounce rate — should stay under 2% per send; spike above that and pause to clean your list
  • Spam complaint rate — anything above 0.1% warrants immediate investigation
  • Open rate by domain — a sudden drop in Gmail or Outlook opens often signals a filtering issue before it becomes a full block
  • Sending velocity — ramping too fast during a seasonal push can trigger rate limiting, especially on newer sending IPs

MailClaw can also automatically pause a sequence if complaint rates breach a threshold you set, which protects your sender reputation during the critical holiday window when you need your domain health intact for multiple consecutive campaigns.

Cloning and Maintaining Your Template Library

The real compounding value of building seasonal templates properly is what happens in year two. Cloning a sequence in MailClaw takes one command:

openclaw sequence clone \
  --source "seasonal-blackfriday-base" \
  --name "seasonal-blackfriday-2025" \
  --update campaign.start_date="2025-11-28" \
  --update campaign.end_date="2025-12-01" \
  --update offer.discount="30%"

Update three variables, review the AI-refreshed copy, check your segment assignments, and you're ready to schedule — in under an hour, for a campaign that might have taken a full week to build from scratch.

Tag your templates consistently (seasonal, template, and the event name) so they're easy to find in the dashboard. And document your variable schema in a shared note or README — especially if others on your team will be working with the same templates. A well-maintained template library is one of the highest-leverage assets your email program can have.

Seasonal email doesn't have to mean seasonal chaos. Build the structure once, let MailClaw's AI agents and sequence builder do the heavy lifting, and spend your campaign energy on the strategy and offers that actually move the needle.

articles.title: Building Automated Upsell Sequences with MailClaw
articles.author: James Rodriguez
articles.summary: Learn how to build intelligent, revenue-driving upsell email sequences using MailClaw's AI email agents, sequence builder, and contact enrichment — all running locally on your Mac with full control over your data and deliverability.
articles.content:
Why Upsell Sequences Are Worth Getting Right

Most revenue growth doesn't come from acquiring new customers — it comes from selling more to the ones you already have. Upsell sequences, when done well, feel less like sales emails and more like timely, helpful nudges that match where a customer actually is in their journey. When done poorly, they feel like spam with a discount code slapped on top.

The difference between those two outcomes usually comes down to timing, personalization, and relevance. That's exactly where an AI-powered local automation tool like MailClaw earns its keep. Because MailClaw runs entirely on your machine at localhost:3100, your customer data never touches a third-party server, and you have complete control over every variable in your sequences — from send timing to AI-generated copy variations.

In this guide, we'll walk through how to build a practical, high-converting upsell sequence using MailClaw's sequence builder, contact enrichment pipeline, and AI email agents — and how to keep deliverability healthy the whole way through.

Planning Your Upsell Sequence Before Touching the Tool

Before you open the MailClaw dashboard, do the strategic work first. A well-planned sequence is far easier to build, and far more effective once it's live.

Define the Trigger Condition

Every upsell sequence needs a clear entry trigger. Common examples include:

  • A customer has been on a starter plan for 30+ days with high usage
  • A contact purchased Product A but hasn't purchased the complementary Product B
  • A user hit a feature limit in your app three times this month
  • A HubSpot or Salesforce deal reached a specific pipeline stage

The more behavioral your trigger, the better. Usage-based triggers outperform time-based ones because they reflect intent. A customer who just hit their storage limit is far more receptive to a storage upgrade than someone who signed up 30 days ago and may be barely engaged.

Map the Sequence Arc

A three-to-five email arc works well for most upsell scenarios. Here's a solid starting framework:

  1. Email 1 — The Awareness Touch: Highlight what they're missing or approaching (no hard sell yet)
  2. Email 2 — The Value Proof: Share a case study, ROI stat, or social proof from a customer at the next tier
  3. Email 3 — The Offer: Present the upgrade with a clear, frictionless CTA
  4. Email 4 — The Urgency Nudge: Time-limited incentive or highlight of a cost they're incurring by not upgrading
  5. Email 5 — The Graceful Exit: Acknowledge they may not be ready and offer a helpful resource instead

This arc respects the customer's timeline while still moving them through a deliberate decision process.

Setting Up MailClaw for Your Upsell Campaign

Importing and Enriching Your Contact Segment

Start by pulling your target segment from your CRM. MailClaw supports direct integrations with HubSpot and Salesforce, so if your data lives there, you can sync contacts straight into a campaign without exporting CSVs manually.

From the terminal, initialize your campaign and pull the contact list:

mailclaw campaign create --name "Q3 Pro Upsell" --type upsell
mailclaw contacts sync --source hubspot --filter "plan=starter&usage_pct>80"

Once your contacts are imported, run MailClaw's contact enrichment pipeline. This step uses OpenClaw's AI layer to fill in missing firmographic data, infer company size, identify likely decision-makers, and flag contacts who may have changed roles — all locally, without sending your data anywhere.

mailclaw enrich --campaign "Q3 Pro Upsell" --fields company_size,role,linkedin_url,tech_stack

Enriched contacts give your AI email agents much more to work with when generating personalized copy. A contact at a 200-person SaaS company gets a different email than a solo founder, even if they're both on the same starter plan.

Configuring Your Sending Accounts

MailClaw supports multi-account sending, which matters for upsell sequences because you often want emails coming from a customer success rep or account manager, not a generic marketing alias. Connect your accounts via OAuth (Gmail and Outlook are both supported) or configure SMTP credentials for SendGrid or Postmark:

mailclaw accounts add --provider gmail --oauth
mailclaw accounts add --provider sendgrid --smtp --api-key YOUR_KEY

For upsell sequences, sending from a named human account significantly improves reply rates. Use MailClaw's multi-account rotation to spread volume across accounts and avoid triggering spam filters.

Building the Sequence in MailClaw

Using the Sequence Builder

Open the local dashboard at localhost:3100 and navigate to Sequences → New Sequence. Select your campaign as the audience source, then start adding steps. Each step lets you define:

  • Delay from previous step (in hours or days)
  • Send window (e.g., weekdays only, 9am–11am recipient local time)
  • Subject line with dynamic variables
  • Email body — written manually or AI-generated
  • Exit conditions (e.g., stop if contact replies or clicks upgrade link)

Exit conditions are critical for upsell sequences. If someone upgrades after Email 2, they absolutely should not receive Email 3's "here's why you should upgrade" message. MailClaw handles this automatically when you configure a goal conversion event.

Activating AI Email Agents for Personalization

This is where MailClaw's OpenClaw-powered AI email agents do their best work. Rather than writing one static email that goes to everyone, you can let the AI agent generate a personalized variant for each contact based on their enriched profile data.

In the sequence builder, toggle AI Agent Mode on for any step, then set your intent and constraints:

mailclaw sequence step add \
  --sequence "Q3 Pro Upsell" \
  --step 2 \
  --mode ai-agent \
  --intent "value proof, highlight ROI of upgrading to Pro" \
  --tone "professional, conversational, no jargon" \
  --max-words 180 \
  --personalize-on "company_size,role,industry"

The AI agent will generate a unique email body for each contact, grounding its copy in the variables you've enriched. A VP of Engineering at a fintech company gets a message that speaks to compliance and team scalability. A founder at an early-stage startup gets something that emphasizes speed and cost-efficiency. Same sequence step, meaningfully different emails.

Pro tip: Review a sample of AI-generated emails before activating a sequence. MailClaw's dashboard lets you preview 10–20 generated variants in the AI Preview Panel. Look for tone consistency and flag any outputs that drift from your brand voice — then tighten your prompt constraints accordingly.

Monitoring Deliverability Throughout the Sequence

An upsell sequence that lands in spam is worse than no sequence at all — it burns sender reputation and trains spam filters against your domain. MailClaw's built-in deliverability tools give you real-time visibility into what's happening at every step.

Pre-Send Checks

Before activating the sequence, run a deliverability audit:

mailclaw deliverability check --campaign "Q3 Pro Upsell" --full

This checks your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, scores your email content for spam trigger language, verifies that your sending domains are warmed up, and estimates inbox placement rates per provider (Gmail, Outlook, etc.).

Live Monitoring During the Sequence

Once the sequence is live, watch the Deliverability Monitor in the localhost dashboard. Key metrics to track:

  • Open rate by step: A sudden drop at Step 3 usually signals a subject line problem, not a deliverability issue
  • Bounce rate: Keep hard bounces below 0.5% — MailClaw will auto-suppress hard bounces by default
  • Spam complaint rate: Anything above 0.1% should trigger an immediate pause and review
  • Reply rate: Replies signal engagement to ISPs and actively improve sender reputation

MailClaw's deliverability tools will surface anomalies automatically and can pause a sequence if complaint rates spike past a threshold you configure — protecting your sender reputation without requiring manual babysitting.

Iterating Based on Results

After your first sequence run, use MailClaw's built-in analytics to identify where contacts are dropping off and where conversions are happening. If Email 3 (the offer) has a high click rate but low conversion, the problem is likely downstream — your landing page or pricing page, not the email itself. If Email 1 has a low open rate, test subject line variants using MailClaw's A/B testing feature before your next batch.

Because MailClaw is open source and built on OpenClaw, you can also extend its behavior programmatically. Teams comfortable with code often pipe sequence analytics into custom dashboards or trigger external webhooks — for example, notifying a Slack channel when a contact enters the final step without converting, so a human can reach out personally.

Putting It All Together

Automated upsell sequences work best when they combine behavioral precision, genuine personalization, and careful deliverability hygiene. MailClaw gives you all three in a single tool that runs locally, keeps your data private, and gives you full transparency into every layer of the system.

Start with a focused segment, let the AI email agents handle personalization at scale, watch your deliverability metrics closely, and iterate quickly. The first sequence you build won't be perfect — but with MailClaw's feedback loop, each subsequent one will convert meaningfully better.

articles.title: How to Use MailClaw for Webinar Promotion Email Sequences
articles.author: Priya Patel
articles.summary: Learn how to build high-converting webinar promotion email sequences using MailClaw's AI email agents, sequence builder, and contact enrichment tools — all running locally on your Mac with zero data leaving your machine.
articles.content:
Why Webinar Promotion Sequences Deserve More Than a Single Blast

Most webinar promotions fail not because the webinar itself is bad, but because the email strategy behind it is lazy. A single "join us Thursday!" blast sent two days before the event leaves registrations on the table, burns goodwill with your list, and gives you almost no data to work with afterward. A properly sequenced campaign — one that nurtures curiosity, handles objections, and follows up with non-attendees — can double your show-up rate and extend the value of a 60-minute webinar for weeks.

MailClaw gives you everything you need to build that kind of sequence without stitching together five different SaaS tools. Because it runs entirely on your Mac at localhost:3100, your contact data and email logic never touch a third-party server. Let's walk through how to set up a complete webinar promotion sequence from scratch.

Planning Your Sequence Architecture

Before you open the dashboard, sketch out the email journey. A solid webinar promotion sequence typically has three phases:

  • Awareness phase — Announce the webinar, establish the value proposition, and drive initial registrations (7–14 days out)
  • Nurture phase — Build anticipation, share social proof, and handle common objections (3–6 days out)
  • Urgency phase — Last-chance reminders, day-of logistics, and live follow-up (24 hours before through 48 hours after)

Within each phase, you'll branch based on behavior: did they register? Did they open the last email? Did they click the registration link but not convert? MailClaw's sequence builder handles all of this branching logic natively, so you define it once and let it run.

Setting Up MailClaw for Your Webinar Campaign

Starting the Local Dashboard

If you haven't already launched MailClaw, fire it up from your terminal:

mailclaw start
# Dashboard available at http://localhost:3100

Once the dashboard loads, navigate to Campaigns → New Campaign and select Webinar Promotion from the template library. This scaffolds a pre-built sequence structure you can customize rather than building from a blank canvas.

Connecting Your Sending Accounts

MailClaw supports multi-account sending through both SMTP and OAuth, so you can connect Gmail, Outlook, or a dedicated sending domain through SendGrid or Postmark. For webinar promotion specifically, we recommend using a sending address on your primary domain — something like events@yourcompany.com — rather than a cold outreach subdomain. Webinar audiences already know your brand, so you want that trust signal in the From field.

To add an account via OAuth (Gmail example):

mailclaw accounts add --provider gmail --oauth
# Follow the browser prompt to authenticate
# Your credentials are stored locally and never synced externally

For SendGrid SMTP, you can add it directly through the dashboard under Settings → Sending Accounts → Add SMTP, or via CLI:

mailclaw accounts add \
  --name "SendGrid Events" \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --user apikey \
  --pass YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY

Enriching Your Contact List Before You Send

Raw registrant lists from Eventbrite, Zoom, or your CRM are rarely complete. You might have an email address and a first name, but knowing someone's job title, company size, or industry lets you personalize messaging in ways that actually move the needle.

MailClaw's contact enrichment layer, powered by OpenClaw, can fill these gaps automatically before your sequence kicks off. Import your base list as a CSV, then run enrichment from the CLI:

mailclaw contacts import --file registrants.csv
mailclaw contacts enrich --campaign webinar-q3 --fields title,company,industry

The enrichment process runs locally using OpenClaw's AI layer, pulling from public data signals and your existing CRM connections (HubSpot, Salesforce, and Pipedrive integrations are all supported). Once complete, you'll see enriched profiles in the contact view at localhost:3100/contacts and can use those fields as personalization tokens throughout your sequence.

Pro tip: Segment enriched contacts by seniority before your sequence launches. A VP-level registrant might respond better to ROI-focused messaging, while an individual contributor might care more about tactical takeaways. MailClaw lets you fork sequence branches by any enriched field.

Building the Email Sequence

The Announcement Email (Day 0)

Your first email should do one thing: make people excited to register. Keep it tight. Lead with the outcome — what will someone be able to do after attending that they can't do now? — and follow with a single CTA button linked to your registration page.

In the sequence builder, set this as your trigger email and configure the branching logic:

  • If contact registers → move to Registered branch
  • If contact opens but doesn't register within 48 hours → send follow-up variant
  • If contact doesn't open within 72 hours → send with alternate subject line

Using AI Email Agents to Write Variants

Writing five or six variations of the same message manually is tedious. MailClaw's AI email agents — built on the OpenClaw engine — can generate subject line variants, rewrite email body copy for different audience segments, and suggest send-time optimizations based on your historical open data.

To generate subject line variants for your announcement email:

mailclaw agent run email-writer \
  --tone professional \
  --goal "webinar registration" \
  --context "B2B SaaS webinar on AI-powered reporting, 45 minutes, free" \
  --output subject-variants.txt

The agent returns five to ten subject line options ranked by predicted open rate. You can pipe the output directly into your sequence draft or review them in the dashboard's built-in editor.

The Registered Confirmation Branch

Everyone who registers should immediately receive a confirmation email with calendar links (Google Calendar, Outlook, and iCal formats), the webinar link, and a one-sentence reminder of what they're going to learn. MailClaw's sequence builder lets you trigger this instantly via a webhook from Zoom, GoToWebinar, or a Zapier integration — no manual work required.

Nurture Emails: Days 3–5

This is where most teams drop the ball. The registrant signed up, got a confirmation, and then heard nothing until the day-of reminder. Use this window to deepen commitment. Good options include:

  • A "what to expect" email walking through the agenda
  • A short case study or testimonial from someone who applied what you'll be teaching
  • A question-prompt email ("What's your biggest challenge with X? Hit reply — we may address it live")

Day-Of and Post-Webinar Emails

Schedule a reminder 2 hours before and another 15 minutes before. For the post-webinar sequence, branch on attendance:

  • Attendees → Thank you email with recording link, key takeaways, and a soft CTA
  • No-shows → "You missed it, here's the replay" email with a subject line that acknowledges the miss without guilt-tripping

Monitoring Deliverability Throughout the Campaign

A webinar promotion sequence sends a high volume of email in a compressed time window, which can trigger spam filters if your sending reputation isn't solid. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring dashboard at localhost:3100/deliverability gives you real-time visibility into bounce rates, spam complaints, and inbox placement estimates.

Set up delivery alerts before your campaign launches:

mailclaw monitor set \
  --campaign webinar-q3 \
  --alert bounce-rate:2% \
  --alert complaint-rate:0.1% \
  --notify slack:#email-alerts

If bounce rates spike — often a sign of a stale list — you can pause the sequence, clean the affected segment, and resume without losing your sequence state. This kind of control is difficult to get in hosted platforms where pausing a live campaign can mean losing progress or triggering contract-level support tickets.

Measuring What Worked

After the webinar, pull a campaign performance report directly from the CLI:

mailclaw report generate \
  --campaign webinar-q3 \
  --metrics opens,clicks,registrations,attendance,replies \
  --format html \
  --output q3-webinar-report.html

The report maps each email in the sequence to downstream outcomes, so you can see not just which email got the most opens, but which email drove the most actual registrations and show-ups. That's the data you need to improve your next campaign — not vanity metrics.

Putting It Together

Webinar promotion isn't glamorous work, but a well-built sequence is a legitimate business asset. Once you've built and optimized it in MailClaw, you can export the entire sequence template — including branching logic, AI-generated variants, and enrichment rules — and reuse it for every future webinar with minimal adjustments.

Because MailClaw is open source and runs locally, you own the entire stack. Your contact data, your sequence logic, your deliverability history — none of it lives in a vendor's cloud waiting to be sunset, price-hiked, or breached. That's a meaningful advantage for any team running serious email programs.

Start with the template, customize the branching logic for your audience, let the AI email agents handle copy variants, and watch your show-up rates climb.

articles.title: MailClaw for Recruiting: Automated Candidate Outreach Sequences
articles.author: Mike Chen
articles.summary: Learn how to use MailClaw's AI email agents, sequence builder, and contact enrichment tools to run automated candidate outreach campaigns that feel personal, respect deliverability, and help you hire faster.
articles.content:
Why Recruiting Outreach Is Broken — And How Automation Fixes It

Recruiting coordinators and talent acquisition teams face a paradox: the best candidates are almost never actively looking, which means you have to reach them cold. But cold outreach at volume is brutally time-consuming when done manually, and most bulk email tools make your messages look exactly like what they are — bulk email.

MailClaw changes the equation. Because it runs locally on your Mac at localhost:3100, your outreach stays private, your candidate data never touches a third-party server, and you maintain full control over every sequence, persona, and sending account. Powered by OpenClaw, MailClaw's AI layer handles the parts that used to require hours of copywriting — while your sequences, timing, and follow-up logic run automatically in the background.

This guide walks through a complete recruiting workflow: building a candidate list, enriching contacts, writing an AI-assisted sequence, and monitoring deliverability so your messages actually land in inboxes.

Setting Up MailClaw for a Recruiting Campaign

Connecting Your Sending Accounts

Recruiting outreach typically works best from a human-looking sender — a real recruiter's Gmail or Outlook account, not a marketing alias. MailClaw supports both OAuth (Gmail, Outlook) and direct SMTP credentials, so you can connect multiple accounts and rotate sending across them to stay within daily limits.

From your local dashboard, navigate to Settings → Email Accounts and click Add Account. For Gmail, authorize via OAuth in a few clicks. For Outlook or a corporate Exchange account, drop in your SMTP host, port, and credentials:

# MailClaw CLI — add an SMTP account
mailclaw account add \
  --name "Sarah (Talent Team)" \
  --smtp-host smtp.office365.com \
  --smtp-port 587 \
  --user sarah@yourcompany.com \
  --pass "your-app-password" \
  --daily-limit 80

Set conservative daily limits per account. For cold outreach, 50–100 emails per day per account is a safe starting range. MailClaw's deliverability monitor will flag you if bounce rates or spam complaints climb above safe thresholds.

Importing and Enriching Your Candidate List

Most recruiters start with a CSV — exported from LinkedIn Recruiter, scraped from GitHub, or pulled from an ATS like Greenhouse or Lever. MailClaw accepts CSV imports directly and can sync contacts from HubSpot or Salesforce if your team tracks candidates there.

# Import candidates from CSV
mailclaw contacts import \
  --file ./senior-engineers-q3.csv \
  --tag "engineering" \
  --tag "senior" \
  --campaign "backend-hiring-q3"

Once imported, run MailClaw's contact enrichment step. The enrichment engine uses OpenClaw to pull publicly available signals — GitHub activity, recent conference talks, open-source contributions, job titles — and appends them to each contact record. This data feeds directly into personalized email copy later.

# Enrich a tagged segment
mailclaw contacts enrich \
  --tag "engineering" \
  --sources github,linkedin-public \
  --output enriched-candidates.json

After enrichment, open your dashboard at localhost:3100/contacts to review the results. You'll see each candidate's enriched profile alongside a readiness score MailClaw assigns based on data completeness — the higher the score, the more personalized your outreach can be.

Building a Candidate Outreach Sequence

Designing the Sequence Structure

A strong cold recruiting sequence has three to five touches spread over two to three weeks. More than that and you risk annoying candidates; fewer and you leave easy responses on the table. Here's a proven structure for technical recruiting:

  • Day 1 — Initial outreach: Short, specific, focused on why this person caught your eye. No attachments, no lengthy pitch.
  • Day 4 — Value-add follow-up: Share something genuinely useful — a blog post, a salary benchmark, or a note about a specific project the candidate might find interesting.
  • Day 9 — Soft bump: A one-liner that acknowledges they're busy and keeps the door open. No pressure.
  • Day 16 — Final check-in: Mention that you'll stop reaching out after this. Often the highest-converting touch in the sequence.

In the MailClaw sequence builder (at localhost:3100/sequences), create a new sequence and add each step with its delay, subject line, and body. You can set exit conditions — if a candidate replies or clicks a calendar link, they exit the sequence automatically so you're never sending a follow-up to someone you're already talking to.

Writing Emails with the AI Email Agent

This is where MailClaw's AI email agent earns its keep. Instead of writing one generic template and calling it personalization, the agent generates per-contact variations using the enriched data you collected earlier.

From the sequence editor, open the AI agent panel for Step 1 and give it a prompt like this:

"Write a concise cold outreach email from a recruiter at a Series B fintech company. The candidate is a senior backend engineer. Reference their most recent open-source project or GitHub contribution if available. Keep it under 100 words. Tone: direct, human, no corporate buzzwords. End with a low-friction CTA — a 15-minute call or async video intro."

The AI agent generates a base template and then, at send time, substitutes real enrichment data for each contact. A candidate who recently merged a notable PR to an open-source database project might receive:

"Hi Marcus — saw your recent work on the connection pooling rewrite in pgbouncer-ng. Impressive approach to the timeout edge cases. We're building similar infrastructure at [Company] and I think you'd find the problem space interesting. Worth a 15-minute call this week?"

That level of specificity is what separates a 40% reply rate from a 4% one.

Setting Sending Rules and Personalization Fallbacks

Not every contact will have rich enrichment data. MailClaw lets you define fallback logic so the AI agent degrades gracefully — using job title and company name when GitHub data is unavailable, for example. Set this in the sequence settings:

# Sequence config (sequences/backend-hiring-q3.yaml)
personalization:
  primary: github_contribution, recent_talk, open_source_project
  fallback: job_title, current_company
  minimum_fields_required: 2
  skip_contact_if_below_minimum: false
  use_generic_variant_if_below_minimum: true

Deliverability: Keeping Your Outreach Out of Spam

Automated recruiting outreach fails silently when emails hit spam folders. MailClaw's deliverability tools run continuously and surface problems before they become expensive.

Warm-Up and Domain Health

If you're using a new sending domain or a freshly created alias, run the built-in warm-up schedule before launching a full campaign. MailClaw gradually increases send volume over 2–3 weeks while monitoring engagement signals. Check your domain's health score from the dashboard or CLI:

# Check deliverability health
mailclaw deliverability check --account "sarah@yourcompany.com"

# Output:
# Domain age: 847 days ✓
# SPF record: valid ✓
# DKIM: configured ✓
# DMARC: p=quarantine ✓
# Blacklist status: clean ✓
# Estimated inbox rate: 94%

Monitoring Bounce and Complaint Rates

MailClaw watches bounce rates per campaign and pauses sequences automatically if they exceed safe thresholds (typically 2% hard bounces). This protects your sender reputation without requiring you to babysit the dashboard. If you're routing through SendGrid or Amazon SES for higher volume, MailClaw pulls webhook data from those services and displays it alongside your native sending stats.

Managing Replies and Handoffs

When a candidate replies, MailClaw's AI email agent can handle first-contact responses for common scenarios — answering basic questions about the role, sending a calendar link, or routing urgent replies to the right recruiter. For more nuanced conversations, the agent flags the reply and surfaces it in your dashboard inbox at localhost:3100/inbox with a suggested reply and the candidate's full enrichment profile alongside.

Positive responses can trigger an automatic tag update and push the contact to your ATS or CRM via MailClaw's native integrations. A quick example for HubSpot:

# Auto-sync interested candidates to HubSpot
mailclaw integrations hubspot sync \
  --trigger "reply_positive" \
  --campaign "backend-hiring-q3" \
  --pipeline "Engineering Candidates" \
  --stage "Recruiter Screen"

Open Source, Local, and Yours

Because MailClaw is open source and runs entirely on your machine, your candidate data never leaves your infrastructure. There's no SaaS vendor storing resumes, email addresses, or conversation histories on your behalf. For recruiting teams at companies with strict data handling policies — especially those hiring for roles with security clearance requirements or in regulated industries — this is a meaningful advantage over hosted outreach platforms.

You can extend MailClaw's behavior by writing custom OpenClaw plugins, modifying sequence logic, or hooking into internal APIs. The entire stack is inspectable, forkable, and self-hostable if you want to move from your Mac to a shared team server.

Getting Started Today

The fastest path to your first automated recruiting sequence looks like this:

  1. Install MailClaw and open the dashboard at localhost:3100
  2. Connect a Gmail or Outlook account via OAuth
  3. Import a CSV of 20–30 target candidates and run enrichment
  4. Build a four-step sequence using the AI email agent with a specific, human prompt
  5. Check deliverability health and launch with a daily cap of 30 emails to start
  6. Review replies in the inbox view and iterate on subject lines after day three

Recruiting is fundamentally a relationship business — but the early stages of finding and warming up candidates are pure logistics. MailClaw handles the logistics so you can spend your time on the conversations that actually move candidates through the funnel.

articles.title: How to Create Feedback Collection Email Flows with MailClaw
articles.author: Anna Liu
articles.summary: Learn how to design and deploy feedback collection email flows using MailClaw's sequence builder, AI email agents, and contact enrichment tools — turning passive recipients into active respondents without leaving your local machine.
articles.content:
Why Feedback Flows Deserve More Than a One-Off Email

Most teams treat feedback collection as an afterthought — a single "How did we do?" email that lands in inboxes at random, gets ignored half the time, and produces data too thin to act on. The reality is that feedback collection is a multi-touch process. People respond when they're reminded, when the ask feels personal, and when the timing aligns with their experience of your product or service.

MailClaw's sequence builder and AI email agents let you build feedback flows that actually work — automated, intelligent, locally hosted, and deeply integrated with the tools your team already uses. Here's how to set one up from scratch.

Planning Your Feedback Flow Before You Build

Before you open the MailClaw dashboard at localhost:3100, spend five minutes thinking through three things:

  • The trigger: What event should kick off the flow? A completed purchase, a closed support ticket, a product onboarding milestone, or a subscription anniversary?
  • The depth of feedback: Are you collecting a quick NPS score, a detailed CSAT survey, or open-ended qualitative input?
  • The fallback: What happens if someone doesn't respond to the first email? How many follow-ups are appropriate before you stop?

A well-designed feedback flow typically looks like this: an initial ask → one or two gentle follow-ups for non-responders → a closing message that thanks responders and lets non-responders gracefully exit the sequence. MailClaw handles all of this natively.

Setting Up MailClaw for Feedback Campaigns

Connect Your Sending Account

MailClaw supports SMTP and OAuth integrations out of the box. If you're sending through Gmail or Outlook, OAuth is the fastest path — it handles token refresh automatically and keeps deliverability stable. For higher-volume campaigns or transactional flows, connect a dedicated SendGrid or Postmark account via SMTP.

From your terminal, initialize a new account connection:

mailclaw account add \
  --name "Feedback Campaigns" \
  --provider gmail \
  --auth oauth \
  --alias feedback@yourcompany.com

Once connected, the account appears in your dashboard under Accounts → Active. You can set sending limits, warm-up schedules, and bounce thresholds all from this panel — critical if you're sending feedback requests at scale and want to protect your domain reputation.

Import and Enrich Your Contact List

MailClaw's contact enrichment layer, powered by OpenClaw, does more than fill in missing fields. It analyzes engagement history, pulls in firmographic data from connected CRMs like HubSpot or Salesforce, and flags contacts who have recently interacted with your product — making them higher-priority targets for feedback requests.

Import a CSV of recent customers and trigger enrichment in one command:

mailclaw contacts import ./recent-customers.csv \
  --enrich \
  --tag "feedback-eligible" \
  --crm hubspot

After enrichment, you'll see each contact's engagement score, last activity date, and any open support tickets pulled in from your CRM. Use these signals to segment your list before the sequence runs — people who just had a negative support interaction might need a different message tone than enthusiastic power users.

Building the Feedback Sequence

Creating the Sequence in the Dashboard

Navigate to localhost:3100/sequences and click New Sequence. Name it something descriptive like "Post-Onboarding Feedback — Q3." Select your enriched contact segment and your connected sending account.

A solid three-step feedback sequence looks like this:

  1. Day 0 — The Ask: Sent immediately after the trigger event. Keep it short, personal, and low-friction. Link directly to your survey tool — Typeform, Notion, Google Forms, or even a plain reply-based format.
  2. Day 4 — The Nudge (non-responders only): A brief follow-up that acknowledges they've been busy and reiterates the value of their input. MailClaw automatically suppresses this step for anyone who clicked or replied in step one.
  3. Day 9 — The Close: Either a thank-you to responders or a graceful exit message for non-responders. Both versions can be handled in the same step using conditional branching.

Writing Emails That Actually Get Responses

This is where MailClaw's AI email agents become genuinely useful. Rather than writing a generic template, let the agent draft personalized copy based on each contact's enrichment data — their role, company size, recent activity, and how long they've been a customer.

mailclaw agent run \
  --task "draft-feedback-sequence" \
  --segment "feedback-eligible" \
  --tone "warm, conversational" \
  --context "post-onboarding, B2B SaaS" \
  --steps 3

The agent will generate three email drafts per contact variation (or per segment persona), which you can review and edit directly in the sequence builder. You're not handing over final send authority to the AI — you're using it to eliminate the blank-page problem and ensure messaging stays contextually relevant.

Pro tip: Ask the AI agent to generate subject line variants for A/B testing on step one. Subject lines like "Quick question about your first week" consistently outperform generic "We'd love your feedback" phrasing — but the winning variant depends heavily on your audience. Test it.

Adding Conditional Logic

MailClaw's sequence builder supports conditional branching based on email events: opens, clicks, replies, and link-specific clicks. For feedback flows, the most useful conditions are:

  • If clicked survey link → remove from sequence, tag as "responded"
  • If replied → pause sequence, notify team via webhook
  • If no open after 4 days → send nudge with different subject line

Configure these in the sequence builder's visual flow editor, or define them in a YAML config file for version control:

steps:
  - id: initial-ask
    delay: 0
    template: feedback-ask-v1
    conditions:
      - event: link_click
        url_contains: "survey"
        action: exit_sequence
        tag: responded
      - event: reply
        action: pause_sequence
        notify: webhook://your-slack-hook

  - id: nudge
    delay: 4
    send_to: unopened
    template: feedback-nudge-v1

  - id: close
    delay: 9
    template: feedback-close-v1

Monitoring Deliverability and Response Rates

A feedback flow only works if your emails actually land in inboxes. MailClaw's built-in deliverability monitoring checks SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment for every connected sending domain and flags issues before a campaign goes live. You'll find this under Deliverability → Domain Health in your local dashboard.

For feedback-specific performance, track these metrics in the campaign analytics panel:

  • Step 1 open rate: Benchmark is 35–50% for well-segmented post-interaction lists. Below 25% means your subject line or sender name needs work.
  • Survey click rate: Aim for 15–25% of recipients clicking through to the survey. A one-click rating embedded directly in the email (like an NPS scale rendered as linked numbers) consistently doubles this.
  • Reply rate on step 2: If your nudge is generating more replies than your initial ask, your follow-up copy is stronger — rewrite the first email.

Connecting Responses Back to Your CRM

Collecting feedback is only half the job. Once responses come in — whether via survey link or direct reply — you want that data flowing back into HubSpot, Salesforce, or whatever CRM your team lives in. MailClaw's webhook and native integration support makes this straightforward.

mailclaw integrations connect hubspot \
  --sync-event reply \
  --sync-event link_click \
  --map "contact.feedback_score → NPS Score" \
  --map "contact.tags → Contact Tags"

With this in place, every survey click and reply automatically updates the contact record in HubSpot — no manual exports, no stale spreadsheets. Your sales and success teams see feedback data in context, right next to deal history and support tickets.

Scaling and Iterating

Because MailClaw is open source and runs locally, your sequence configs, templates, and enrichment rules are all plain files you can version control in Git. This makes iteration fast — update a template, push the change, and the next batch of contacts gets the improved version. No vendor portal, no support ticket, no waiting.

Once your feedback flow is producing consistent response rates, consider spinning up a dedicated AI email agent that monitors incoming replies, categorizes sentiment, and triggers follow-up actions automatically — routing negative feedback to your support queue and positive responses to your testimonial pipeline. That's a topic for its own post, but the foundation you've built here is exactly where it starts.

Feedback collection doesn't have to be a guessing game or a manual chore. With MailClaw handling the sequencing, personalization, deliverability, and CRM sync, the only thing you need to focus on is what you actually do with what people tell you.

articles.title: Building Partnership Outreach Sequences with MailClaw AI
articles.author: David Torres
articles.summary: Learn how to build high-converting partnership outreach sequences using MailClaw's AI email agents, contact enrichment, and sequence builder — with step-by-step CLI commands and practical templates you can deploy today.
articles.content:
Why Partnership Outreach Is Different (And Harder)

Cold sales outreach is transactional. Partnership outreach is relational. You're not asking someone to buy something — you're asking them to bet a piece of their brand, audience, or pipeline on working with you. That means the bar for relevance, personalization, and timing is significantly higher.

Most partnership sequences fail for one of three reasons: they're too generic, they're sent to the wrong person, or they give up after one or two touches. MailClaw's AI-powered toolchain addresses all three of these problems directly — and because it runs locally on your Mac at localhost:3100, you're never handing sensitive contact data to a third-party SaaS platform you don't control.

Setting Up Your Partnership Campaign in MailClaw

1. Launch the Local Dashboard and Create a Campaign

Start by spinning up MailClaw and opening the dashboard. If you've already installed via Homebrew or cloned the repo, it's a single command:

openclaw start --service mailclaw
# Dashboard available at http://localhost:3100

From the dashboard, navigate to Campaigns → New Campaign and select Partnership Outreach as your campaign type. This pre-loads a set of AI prompts and sequence logic tuned for relationship-building rather than conversion-first messaging. Give your campaign a name, connect your sending account (Gmail OAuth and Outlook OAuth are both supported), and set your daily send limits before you do anything else.

2. Build Your Target Contact List

Partnership outreach lives or dies by list quality. A spray-and-pray approach will tank your deliverability and waste the goodwill of people who might have been real partners someday.

MailClaw's contact enrichment engine, powered by the OpenClaw AI core, can take a raw list of company domains or LinkedIn URLs and return enriched contact records including:

  • Decision-maker name and verified work email
  • Company size, industry, and tech stack
  • Recent news mentions and funding events
  • Social proof signals (podcast appearances, newsletter audience size, etc.)

To enrich a CSV of target companies from the CLI:

mailclaw contacts enrich \
  --input ./partners-raw.csv \
  --fields name,email,company_size,tech_stack,recent_news \
  --output ./partners-enriched.csv

This enriched data feeds directly into the AI personalization layer when you build your sequence. The difference between "I'd love to explore a partnership" and "I saw you just closed your Series A and are expanding into enterprise — we've helped three similar companies build co-marketing programs that drove 20% of their new ARR" is the data behind the message.

Designing the Sequence Architecture

The 5-Touch Partnership Framework

Partnership relationships require more patience than sales sequences. Rushing a "yes" before trust is established rarely works. Here's the framework that tends to perform well, which you can implement directly in MailClaw's sequence builder:

  1. Touch 1 (Day 1) — The Warm Opener: Short, specific, no ask. Reference something real about their business. End with a soft question, not a calendar link.
  2. Touch 2 (Day 4) — The Value Add: Share a resource, case study, or insight genuinely relevant to their situation. No pitch yet.
  3. Touch 3 (Day 9) — The Soft Pitch: Introduce the partnership idea with one concrete mutual benefit. Include social proof. Offer a low-friction next step.
  4. Touch 4 (Day 15) — The Follow-Up: Brief check-in that acknowledges they're busy and restates the core value prop in one sentence.
  5. Touch 5 (Day 22) — The Graceful Exit: Close the loop. Either resurface interest or give them an easy out — either outcome is fine.

In the MailClaw sequence builder, you can configure each step's delay, channel (email, optionally paired with LinkedIn touch reminders), and the AI personalization variables to inject at each stage.

Configuring the AI Email Agent

This is where MailClaw genuinely separates itself. Rather than writing five static templates and blasting them, you configure an AI email agent that generates personalized variations of each touch based on the enriched contact data.

From the CLI, define your agent for this campaign:

mailclaw agent create \
  --campaign "q3-partnerships-2024" \
  --persona "partnership-outreach" \
  --tone professional-warm \
  --variables "{{contact.first_name}},{{contact.company}},{{contact.recent_news}},{{contact.tech_stack}}" \
  --sequence-steps 5

The agent uses each contact's enriched profile to make every email feel like it was written specifically for that person — because, functionally, it was. You can review and approve generated drafts in bulk from the dashboard before anything goes out, which is the workflow most teams prefer.

Pro tip: Create a "persona" file that captures your company's voice, the specific partnership types you're pursuing, and two or three example emails you've written manually that performed well. The AI agent learns from these examples and stays consistent with your brand voice across all 5 touches.

Protecting Deliverability Across a Partnership Campaign

Partnership outreach often involves reaching people at companies where you have no prior relationship — which means inbox placement is not guaranteed. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring tools give you real-time visibility into what's happening.

Key Deliverability Settings to Configure

  • Sending volume ramp: If you're using a new Gmail or Outlook account, use MailClaw's warmup scheduler to gradually increase volume over 2–3 weeks before launching your full sequence.
  • Bounce and reply detection: Set up automatic sequence pausing when a contact bounces or replies — MailClaw handles this natively, but confirm it's enabled per campaign.
  • Domain health monitoring: The dashboard's deliverability panel shows SPF, DKIM, and DMARC status for every connected domain. Fix issues before they compound.
  • Send time optimization: MailClaw can stagger sends across your list based on the recipient's timezone, inferred from enrichment data. Tuesday through Thursday, 9–11am local time consistently outperforms other windows for B2B partnership emails.

If you're sending at higher volumes through a dedicated IP via SendGrid or Postmark, you can configure those SMTP connections directly in MailClaw:

mailclaw smtp add \
  --provider sendgrid \
  --api-key $SENDGRID_API_KEY \
  --from-email partnerships@yourcompany.com \
  --daily-limit 200

Integrating With Your CRM

Partnership conversations don't end in the inbox. Once a prospect replies, you need that context tracked somewhere your team can act on it. MailClaw supports bi-directional sync with HubSpot and Salesforce, as well as webhook-based integration with anything else.

To push contact activity to HubSpot automatically:

mailclaw integrations connect hubspot \
  --api-key $HUBSPOT_KEY \
  --sync-events open,reply,click,bounce \
  --campaign "q3-partnerships-2024"

Now every open, reply, and click from your sequence is logged against the contact record in HubSpot in real time. When a partner prospect replies positively, your business development team sees it in their CRM immediately without any manual data entry.

Reading the Results and Iterating

A partnership sequence is a hypothesis, not a final product. After your first cohort of 50–100 contacts completes all five touches, pull the performance report from the dashboard and look at three things:

  1. Which touch had the highest reply rate? If it's Touch 2 or 3, your opener might be underperforming. Test a more direct subject line on Touch 1.
  2. What's the subject line open rate on Touch 4? A low open rate here suggests subject line fatigue — try breaking the thread with a fresh subject instead of replying inline.
  3. What percentage of positive replies came from enriched vs. non-enriched contacts? This tells you exactly how much ROI the contact enrichment step is generating.

MailClaw's A/B testing module lets you split your next cohort across two agent personas or two sequence frameworks and compare results side by side. Over three or four iterations, most teams get their positive reply rate from the 2–3% range to somewhere between 8–15% for well-targeted partnership lists — which, for a relationship that could drive significant revenue, is an outstanding return on a few hours of setup work.

The Open-Source Advantage

Because MailClaw is open source and built on OpenClaw, you're not locked into anyone's pricing model, API rate limits, or data retention policies. Your enriched contact data, your AI-generated email drafts, your sequence logic, and your campaign analytics all live on your own machine. You can extend the sequence builder, build custom enrichment plugins, or wire in proprietary data sources that a SaaS tool would never support.

For partnership teams at early-stage companies especially, that combination of capability and control is rare — and it's exactly the kind of foundation you want under a program that's meant to build long-term relationships.

articles.title: How to Automate Invoice and Payment Reminder Emails with MailClaw
articles.author: Ahmad Saroya
articles.summary: Learn how to set up automated invoice and payment reminder email sequences using MailClaw, from configuring your first SMTP connection to building multi-step AI-powered follow-up workflows that recover late payments without lifting a finger.
articles.content:
Why Payment Reminders Are Worth Automating

Late invoices are one of the most quietly damaging problems for freelancers and small businesses. According to Atradius, nearly 48% of B2B invoices in the US are paid late — not because clients are malicious, but because invoices get buried, forgotten, or deprioritized. A well-timed, professionally worded reminder is often all it takes.

The problem is that writing those reminders manually is tedious, awkward, and easy to skip when you're busy doing actual work. That's exactly the kind of repetitive, high-value task that MailClaw was built to handle. With its open-source AI backbone powered by OpenClaw, you can set up an entire invoice follow-up system that runs locally on your Mac — no third-party SaaS fees, no data leaving your machine, and no copy-pasting the same email for the fifteenth time.

Setting Up MailClaw for Invoice Workflows

Step 1: Start the Local Dashboard

If you haven't already, spin up MailClaw and open the local dashboard in your browser:

mailclaw start
# Dashboard available at http://localhost:3100

From the dashboard, navigate to Settings → Email Accounts and connect the account you use for client billing. MailClaw supports both SMTP credentials and OAuth2 — so whether you're sending from Gmail, Outlook, or a custom domain via SendGrid or Postmark, the setup is straightforward.

For Gmail via OAuth:

mailclaw account add \
  --provider gmail \
  --auth oauth2 \
  --label "Billing Account"

For a SendGrid SMTP setup:

mailclaw account add \
  --provider smtp \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --user apikey \
  --label "SendGrid Billing"

Step 2: Import or Enrich Your Contacts

MailClaw's contact enrichment feature is genuinely useful here. If you're pulling client data from a CRM like HubSpot or Salesforce, you can import a CSV and let MailClaw fill in the gaps — company size, billing contact name, and even payment history fields if you've mapped them from your invoicing tool.

mailclaw contacts import --file clients.csv --enrich --tag invoicing

The --enrich flag kicks off OpenClaw's enrichment pipeline, which cross-references available data to normalize names, validate email addresses, and flag any contacts with deliverability risks before you send a single message.

Building Your Invoice Reminder Sequence

The real power lives in the sequence builder. A good invoice reminder workflow typically follows a three-stage structure:

  1. Friendly pre-due reminder — sent 3 days before the invoice due date
  2. Due-date nudge — sent on the due date if unpaid
  3. Overdue follow-ups — a graduated series at 7, 14, and 30 days past due

From the dashboard, go to Sequences → New Sequence, or use the CLI to scaffold a new one:

mailclaw sequence create \
  --name "Invoice Follow-Up" \
  --tag invoicing \
  --trigger date_field:due_date

Writing the Email Steps

Here's an example sequence configuration in MailClaw's YAML format, which you can edit directly or through the visual builder in the dashboard:

sequence:
  name: Invoice Follow-Up
  trigger:
    field: due_date
    offset: -3d

  steps:
    - name: Pre-Due Reminder
      delay: 0
      subject: "Your invoice {{invoice_number}} is due on {{due_date}}"
      body: |
        Hi {{first_name}},
