Monitor Engagement Signals Per Step

Inside the MailClaw dashboard, each sequence step shows its own engagement metrics independently. This is powerful because it tells you exactly where your sequence is losing momentum. If Step 3 has a 35% open rate but a 0.4% reply rate, your subject line is working but your body copy is missing the mark. If Step 4 has a sharp drop in opens, prospects may be unsubscribing or filtering after Step 3.

MailClaw also integrates with HubSpot and Salesforce — so engagement events from your sequences can sync back to your CRM as activity records, keeping your sales team's pipeline data current without manual entry.

Multi-Account Sending Strategies

Spreading volume across multiple sending accounts is standard practice for high-volume outreach. MailClaw's multi-account support lets you round-robin sends across Gmail, Outlook, and SMTP accounts from a single sequence configuration:

mailclaw sequence update "Q4 Outreach" \
  --sending-accounts "gmail-primary,gmail-secondary,outlook-sales" \
  --rotation round-robin \
  --daily-limit-per-account 150

This keeps individual account volume low and natural, reducing the risk that any single account triggers automated spam detection. Pair this with unique sending subdomains (outreach1.yourdomain.com, outreach2.yourdomain.com) and you have a resilient sending infrastructure that scales without burning your primary domain.

The Breakup Email: Don't Skip It

The final step of your sequence deserves special attention. A well-written breakup email — honest, low-pressure, and brief — often outperforms every earlier step in terms of reply rate. It works because it removes pressure entirely and gives the prospect a clear off-ramp, which paradoxically makes them more likely to respond.

A simple template that works:

Subject: Should I close your file?

Hi {{first_name}},

I've reached out a few times and haven't heard back — totally understand,
timing isn't always right.

I'll stop following up after this. If things change down the road, you know
where to find me.

Either way, best of luck with {{company}}.

— {{sender_name}}

MailClaw's AI agent can generate breakup email variants tuned to each contact's industry and the specific angle your previous steps took. This keeps even your final touch feeling personalized rather than templated.

Iterate Fast, Measure Everything

The most important practice isn't a specific timing rule or a particular sequence length — it's building a system where you're constantly testing and learning. MailClaw's open-source foundation means you can extend the reporting layer, write custom scripts to pull sequence analytics, and even build your own dashboards on top of the local API.

Start with the framework above, run it for 30 days, then audit your per-step metrics. Double down on what's working, rewrite what isn't, and use the AI email agents to generate fresh variants quickly. Good sequences are built through iteration, not inspiration.

Your localhost dashboard at localhost:3100 keeps everything in one place — contacts, sequences, agents, deliverability, and campaign analytics — so you're never hunting across five tabs to understand what's happening with your outreach. Run mailclaw start, open your browser, and start building.

articles.title: How to Train Your Sales Team on MailClaw Email Automation
articles.author: Sarah Kim
articles.summary: Learn how to onboard and train your sales team on MailClaw's AI-powered email automation features, from setting up the local dashboard to building sequences and coaching reps with real deliverability data.
articles.content:
Why Email Automation Training Is a Sales Multiplier

Most sales teams don't fail at email because they lack effort — they fail because they lack consistency, personalization at scale, and visibility into what's actually working. MailClaw solves all three. But like any powerful tool, it only delivers results when your team knows how to use it properly.

Training your sales team on MailClaw isn't just about showing them where to click. It's about changing how they think about outreach — moving from one-off, gut-feel emails to structured, AI-assisted sequences that run intelligently in the background while reps focus on closing. This guide walks you through exactly how to do that, from first install to full team deployment.

Step 1: Get Everyone Running MailClaw Locally

MailClaw runs on your Mac at localhost:3100 — no cloud subscription, no SaaS dependency, no vendor lock-in. This is a meaningful shift for teams used to browser-based tools. Start training by making sure every rep has a working local instance before you touch anything else.

Installation and First Boot

Have each team member run the following from their terminal:

# Clone and start MailClaw via OpenClaw
npx openclaw install mailclaw

# Start the local server
mailclaw start

# Open the dashboard
open http://localhost:3100

Once they see the dashboard, run a quick orientation session — even 15 minutes on a shared screen call. Cover the main navigation sections: Campaigns, Sequences, Contacts, Agents, and Deliverability. Reps who understand the layout from day one avoid the confusion that derails most tool rollouts.

Connecting Their Email Accounts

MailClaw supports both SMTP and OAuth integration, which means your team can connect Gmail, Outlook, or any custom domain they're already using for sales. Walk each rep through connecting their primary sending account:

  1. Navigate to Settings → Email Accounts in the dashboard
  2. Click Add Account and choose Gmail (OAuth), Outlook (OAuth), or SMTP
  3. For Gmail, authenticate via the standard Google OAuth flow — no app passwords needed
  4. For custom domains sending through SendGrid or Postmark, enter SMTP credentials directly
  5. Send a test email and verify it lands in inbox (not spam) before moving on

Multi-account support means reps can manage a personal outreach address and a shared team alias from the same MailClaw instance — a small feature that saves a surprising amount of daily friction.

Step 2: Build Your First Shared Sequence Together

The best training exercise isn't a demo — it's a live build. Gather your team (in-person or on a call) and build a real sequence together using the Sequence Builder. Pick an actual campaign: a new product announcement, a re-engagement push to cold leads, or a trial conversion sequence.

Anatomy of a Good MailClaw Sequence

Walk the team through what a high-performing sequence looks like in MailClaw before they start clicking:

  • Step 1 — Initial outreach: Short, personalized, clear value proposition. No attachments.
  • Step 2 — Follow-up (Day 3): Reference the first email, add a new angle or social proof.
  • Step 3 — Value add (Day 7): A resource, case study, or relevant insight. No ask.
  • Step 4 — Breakup (Day 14): Low-pressure final touch. Easy to reply to.

Have reps draft the copy for each step directly in the Sequence Builder. Then introduce the AI assist feature — MailClaw's OpenClaw-powered AI can suggest subject line variations, rewrite steps for tone, or generate entirely new steps based on a prompt. Show the team how to use it as a collaborator, not a crutch.

Pro tip for trainers: Ask reps to write their email copy first, then use the AI to improve it — not the other way around. This keeps their voice in the message while still benefiting from AI polish. Sequences that sound robotic get ignored; sequences that sound human get replies.

Step 3: Teach Contact Enrichment Before Any Campaign Goes Live

Garbage in, garbage out. One of the most impactful things you can train your team on is contact enrichment — using MailClaw to fill in missing data on leads before they enter a sequence.

Running Enrichment on a Contact List

From the Contacts section, reps can upload a CSV of leads (exported from HubSpot, Salesforce, or even a raw LinkedIn scrape) and trigger enrichment in one command:

# Enrich a CSV of contacts via CLI
mailclaw enrich --file leads.csv --fields title,company,linkedin,phone

# Or trigger from the dashboard
# Contacts → Import → Enable Enrichment → Run

MailClaw will cross-reference available signals to fill in job titles, company size, LinkedIn URLs, and more. Train reps to review enriched data before launching — not because the enrichment is inaccurate, but because understanding your contacts is what makes personalization feel real rather than automated.

This is also a good moment to show how enriched fields plug directly into sequence templates using variables like {{contact.title}}, {{contact.company}}, and {{contact.first_name}} — keeping every email feeling individually crafted even at scale.

Step 4: Introduce AI Email Agents for Advanced Workflows

Once your team is comfortable with sequences, introduce AI email agents — one of MailClaw's most powerful and most underused features. Agents are autonomous workflows that can monitor replies, classify intent, trigger follow-ups, and even draft responses for rep review.

Setting Up a Basic Reply-Handling Agent

Start with a simple agent: one that watches for positive replies and flags them in the dashboard for immediate rep action. In the Agents section:

  1. Create a new agent and name it (e.g., Interested Reply Watcher)
  2. Set the trigger: Inbound reply received
  3. Add a condition: AI classifies intent as Positive / Interested
  4. Set the action: Notify rep + pause sequence + tag contact as Hot Lead
  5. Optionally: have the agent draft a suggested reply for the rep to approve before sending

This single agent saves reps from manually monitoring inboxes and ensures no warm lead goes cold because someone missed a notification. Train the team to trust the flagging system, but always review agent-drafted replies before sending — AI context is good, human judgment is still better for nuanced conversations.

Step 5: Make Deliverability a Team Habit, Not an Afterthought

Most sales reps have no idea their emails are landing in spam. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring tools change that — but only if you train the team to look at the data.

What to Review in the Deliverability Dashboard

Set a weekly habit: every Monday, reps check their deliverability panel for:

  • Spam rate — anything above 0.1% needs immediate attention
  • Bounce rate — hard bounces should trigger contact cleanup
  • Open rate by domain — low rates from Gmail addresses often signal a reputation issue
  • DKIM/SPF/DMARC status — MailClaw surfaces these clearly; green means go
  • Sending volume trends — sudden spikes can trigger provider throttling

Reps who monitor deliverability proactively consistently outperform those who don't — not because they're more skilled, but because they're sending fewer emails that get ignored or filtered. Train this as a professional habit, not an IT concern.

Building a Culture of Iteration

The final piece of sales team training isn't about MailClaw features at all — it's about mindset. Email automation only compounds in value when teams treat it as a system to improve, not a task to complete.

Establish a monthly review ritual: pull sequence performance data from the dashboard, identify the step with the lowest reply rate, and rewrite it as a team. Run A/B variants where possible. Use the AI to generate three alternative subject lines and test them across cohorts. Share wins openly — when one rep's sequence outperforms, make the template available to everyone.

Because MailClaw is open source and built on OpenClaw, your most technical team members can also extend it — building custom integrations with your CRM, writing enrichment plugins, or connecting it to internal tools via the API. That extensibility means the tool grows with your team rather than boxing you in.

The teams that get the most from MailClaw aren't the ones who learned it fastest — they're the ones who never stopped learning it.

articles.title: MailClaw Governance: Email Compliance Policies for Enterprise Teams
articles.author: James Rodriguez
articles.summary: Learn how enterprise teams can implement robust email compliance policies within MailClaw, covering data governance, consent management, sending limits, and audit trails to keep outreach legal, ethical, and deliverable.
articles.content:
Why Email Governance Matters More Than Ever for Enterprise Teams

Enterprise email outreach sits at a complicated intersection of ambition and accountability. Your sales team wants to send more, your marketing team wants to personalize deeper, and your legal team wants a paper trail for everything. Add in regulations like GDPR, CAN-SPAM, CASL, and the relatively new EU AI Act implications for automated outreach, and it becomes clear that "just blast and hope" is not a strategy — it's a liability.

MailClaw's architecture is uniquely suited for governance-conscious teams. Because it runs locally on your Mac at localhost:3100, your contact data never passes through a third-party SaaS pipeline unless you explicitly configure an integration. That baseline of data locality is a meaningful compliance advantage, especially for organizations under strict data residency requirements. But local control alone isn't enough. You need policies, guardrails, and auditable processes baked into how your team uses the tool.

This guide walks through practical governance frameworks you can implement in MailClaw today — covering consent management, sending limits, team permissions, audit logging, and integration hygiene with tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, Gmail, and SendGrid.

Establishing a Consent Management Framework

Before a single email leaves your SMTP relay or OAuth-connected Gmail account, you need a clear answer to one question: do you have a legitimate legal basis to contact this person? In practice, that means tagging every contact in MailClaw with a consent status before they enter any sequence.

Tagging Contacts at Enrichment Time

MailClaw's contact enrichment pipeline — powered by OpenClaw — is the ideal point to enforce consent tagging. When you enrich a contact from a CSV import, a CRM sync, or a manual entry, you can append custom fields that track consent source and timestamp. A practical schema looks like this:

# Example contact enrichment payload with consent metadata
{
  "email": "jane.doe@acmecorp.com",
  "first_name": "Jane",
  "company": "Acme Corp",
  "enriched_at": "2025-01-15T09:00:00Z",
  "consent": {
    "status": "opt-in",
    "source": "webinar-signup-2025-01",
    "basis": "legitimate_interest",
    "jurisdiction": "EU",
    "expires_at": "2026-01-15T09:00:00Z"
  }
}

Once this schema is standardized across your team, you can build MailClaw sequences that filter on consent status as a prerequisite step. Anyone without a valid consent.status of opt-in or legitimate_interest simply never enters the sequence — no exceptions, no overrides without a supervisor approval trigger.

Syncing Consent State with HubSpot and Salesforce

If your team uses HubSpot or Salesforce as the system of record, MailClaw's CRM integrations can pull consent fields bi-directionally. Set a policy that the CRM field is the canonical source of truth. Any unsubscribe or consent withdrawal processed in MailClaw should write back to Salesforce within a defined SLA — 24 hours is a reasonable enterprise standard. This prevents the scenario where a contact opts out via your CRM portal but continues to receive MailClaw sequences because the suppression list wasn't synchronized.

Defining Sending Limits and Throttle Policies

Volume controls aren't just a deliverability concern — they're a governance mechanism. Unrestricted sending is how well-intentioned campaigns become harassment, and how domain reputations collapse overnight.

Per-Account Daily Send Caps

MailClaw supports multi-account configurations, letting teams connect multiple Gmail, Outlook, or custom SMTP accounts through a single dashboard. Each account should have a documented daily send cap that aligns with its warmup history and your SMTP provider's limits. A sensible enterprise starting point:

  • Freshly warmed Gmail via OAuth: 150–200 emails/day per account
  • Established Outlook/Microsoft 365 account: 300–500 emails/day
  • SendGrid or dedicated SMTP with domain authentication: Scale with reputation, but cap individual campaigns at 2,000/day until deliverability baselines are established

Configure these limits in MailClaw's account settings and treat them as policy, not suggestions. Document the caps in your team's email governance playbook so that new SDRs or marketing coordinators can't accidentally override them through the sequence builder UI.

Sequence-Level Rate Controls

Beyond account caps, individual sequences should have their own throttle settings. In MailClaw's sequence builder, you can define send windows — for example, Monday through Thursday, 8 AM to 5 PM in the recipient's local timezone — and set minimum gaps between touches. A governance-compliant B2B sequence might look like this:

  1. Step 1: Initial outreach email — Day 0
  2. Step 2: Follow-up with value add — Day 4 (minimum 96-hour gap enforced)
  3. Step 3: Case study or social proof — Day 9
  4. Step 4: Break-up email — Day 16 (auto-suppresses contact if no reply by Day 20)

The auto-suppression rule at Step 4 is critical. Contacts who haven't engaged after a full sequence cycle should move to a suppression list, not a re-enrollment queue — at least not without a cooling-off period of 60–90 days and a fresh consent review.

Role-Based Access and Team Permissions

In enterprise environments, not everyone should have the same level of access to MailClaw's capabilities. Your AI email agents are powerful — an agent configured poorly can send thousands of personalized emails before anyone notices something is wrong. Role boundaries prevent that.

Defining a Permission Tier Model

Since MailClaw is open-source and self-hosted, your team has full control over how access is structured. A practical three-tier model for enterprise teams:

  • Viewer: Can see campaign dashboards, deliverability reports, and sequence performance in the localhost dashboard. Cannot create or modify sequences.
  • Contributor: Can build sequences and enrich contacts, but cannot activate a sequence or connect new SMTP/OAuth accounts. All new sequences require Approver sign-off before activation.
  • Approver/Admin: Full access, including AI agent configuration, account management, and suppression list overrides. This role should be limited to 2–3 people per team.

Governance tip: Require a second Approver to review any AI email agent configuration before it goes live. AI agents in MailClaw can autonomously adjust messaging, timing, and follow-up logic — that's their value, but it's also why they need a human sign-off gate in enterprise contexts.

Audit Logging and Deliverability Monitoring as Compliance Tools

Governance without a paper trail isn't governance — it's optimism. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring tools and local logging capabilities give you the foundation for an auditable email program.

What to Log and Where

At a minimum, your enterprise MailClaw deployment should maintain logs for:

  • Every email sent: timestamp, recipient, sequence name, account used, and message ID
  • Every bounce, unsubscribe, or spam complaint with the associated contact record
  • Every consent status change and who triggered it
  • Every AI agent decision that resulted in a schedule change or message variant selection

Because MailClaw runs locally, these logs live on your infrastructure. Pipe them to your existing SIEM or logging platform using a simple log export script:

# Export MailClaw activity logs to a central logging endpoint
mailclaw logs export \
  --from 2025-01-01 \
  --to 2025-01-31 \
  --format json \
  --output /var/log/mailclaw/january-2025.json

# Or stream to a remote endpoint in real time
mailclaw logs stream --webhook https://your-siem.internal/mailclaw-ingest

Using Deliverability Data to Catch Policy Violations Early

MailClaw's deliverability monitoring surfaces bounce rates, spam complaint rates, and inbox placement trends across all connected accounts. Set policy thresholds and treat them as automatic kill switches. A reasonable enterprise policy:

  • If a campaign's bounce rate exceeds 3%, pause it automatically and require an Approver review before resuming
  • If a spam complaint rate on any account exceeds 0.08% (Google's own threshold), suspend that account's sending and audit the sequence that drove the complaints
  • Review deliverability dashboards weekly as part of a standing ops cadence, not just reactively

Building a Living Governance Playbook

The policies above are only as good as their documentation and enforcement. Write them down — not in a lengthy PDF that no one reads, but in a short, versioned governance playbook that lives alongside your MailClaw configuration in your team's internal wiki or Git repository.

Your playbook should cover: consent standards by jurisdiction, approved sequence templates, account send caps, escalation paths when a compliance issue is detected, and a quarterly review cadence to update policies as regulations evolve. Because MailClaw is open-source, you can also commit governance configuration files directly to your repo — making policy changes trackable, reviewable, and reversible like any other piece of infrastructure code.

Email compliance isn't a one-time setup task. It's an ongoing discipline. The teams that handle it well aren't the ones with the most complex systems — they're the ones who made governance a habit early, before a spam complaint or a regulatory inquiry forced their hand.

articles.title: How to Handle Bounced and Invalid Emails in MailClaw
articles.author: Priya Patel
articles.summary: Learn how to detect, categorize, and automatically handle bounced and invalid emails in MailClaw — protecting your sender reputation and keeping your contact lists clean with AI-powered tools.
articles.content:
Why Bounce Management Is Non-Negotiable for Email Deliverability

Every email marketer eventually runs into the same painful reality: a percentage of your carefully crafted emails will never reach a human inbox. They'll bounce. And if you ignore those bounces long enough, inbox providers like Gmail and Outlook will quietly start routing your legitimate emails to spam — or blocking them outright.

Bounce rates above 2% are a red flag for most major email providers. Above 5%, you're in dangerous territory. The good news is that MailClaw — running locally on your Mac at localhost:3100 — gives you a full suite of tools to catch, categorize, and act on bounces automatically, before they compound into a deliverability crisis.

Understanding the Two Types of Email Bounces

Before you can fix bounces, you need to understand what you're dealing with. Not all bounces are created equal.

Hard Bounces

A hard bounce means permanent delivery failure. The email address doesn't exist, the domain is invalid, or the receiving server has explicitly rejected the message with no hope of future delivery. Common causes include:

  • Typos in email addresses (e.g., john@gmial.com)
  • Deactivated or deleted accounts
  • Invalid or expired domains
  • Email addresses that were never real to begin with

Hard bounces should be removed from your lists immediately. There is no scenario where retrying a hard bounce is the right move — it only hurts your sender score.

Soft Bounces

A soft bounce is a temporary failure. The address is valid, but delivery failed for a transient reason. Examples include:

  • Recipient's mailbox is full
  • Receiving server is temporarily down or throttling
  • Message too large for the recipient's settings
  • Greylisting (server temporarily rejected the email as a spam-prevention measure)

Soft bounces warrant a retry — but with limits. MailClaw's sequence builder lets you configure retry logic so you don't hammer a temporarily unreachable address indefinitely.

Setting Up Bounce Tracking in MailClaw

MailClaw handles bounce tracking through your connected sending accounts. Whether you're using Gmail OAuth, Outlook OAuth, or a third-party SMTP provider like SendGrid or Postmark, MailClaw can parse bounce notifications and update your contact records automatically.

Connecting Your Sending Account

From your local dashboard at localhost:3100, navigate to Settings → Sending Accounts and add your account. For SMTP-based providers like SendGrid, you'll want to configure a dedicated bounce webhook endpoint:

# Start MailClaw and expose the bounce webhook
mailclaw serve --port 3100 --enable-webhooks

# Your local bounce webhook will be available at:
# http://localhost:3100/webhooks/bounce

For production use, you'll need to expose this webhook to the public internet using a tunneling tool like ngrok so that SendGrid, Mailgun, or Postmark can POST bounce events to your MailClaw instance.

# Expose your local MailClaw instance via ngrok
ngrok http 3100

# Then configure your SendGrid bounce webhook to:
# https://your-ngrok-id.ngrok.io/webhooks/bounce

Configuring Bounce Rules

Once your webhook is live, open the MailClaw config file to define how different bounce types should be handled:

# ~/.mailclaw/config.yml

bounces:
  hard:
    action: suppress          # Permanently suppress the contact
    notify: true              # Log to dashboard and alert
  soft:
    max_retries: 3            # Retry up to 3 times
    retry_interval: 24h       # Wait 24 hours between retries
    action_on_exceed: pause   # Pause contact after max retries

This configuration means MailClaw will automatically suppress hard-bounced addresses and intelligently retry soft bounces — no manual intervention required.

Using AI-Powered Contact Enrichment to Prevent Bounces

The best bounce is one that never happens. MailClaw's contact enrichment feature, powered by OpenClaw, can validate and enrich email addresses before you send — catching obvious problems at the source.

Running Pre-Send Validation

Before launching a sequence, run the contact enrichment pipeline on your list:

# Validate and enrich a contact list before sending
mailclaw enrich --list contacts.csv --validate-emails --output enriched.csv

# Check the validation report
mailclaw enrich --report enriched.csv

MailClaw's enrichment layer checks DNS records for each domain, validates MX record existence, and flags addresses with known disposable or role-based patterns (like info@ or noreply@) that tend to have high bounce rates. It also cross-references contacts against enrichment data sources to verify that an address is likely active.

Integrating With Your CRM

If you're pulling contacts from HubSpot or Salesforce, MailClaw can sync bounce data back to your CRM automatically. Hard-bounced contacts can be tagged or moved to a suppression list in HubSpot, keeping your CRM data clean alongside your email data:

# Sync bounce suppressions back to HubSpot
mailclaw sync --provider hubspot --action tag-bounced --tag "email-bounced"

Automating Bounce Handling With AI Email Agents

One of MailClaw's most powerful capabilities is its AI email agents — autonomous agents built on OpenClaw that can make intelligent decisions about your campaign contacts without you having to babysit every bounce notification.

Building a Bounce Remediation Agent

You can create a dedicated agent that monitors your bounce queue, attempts to find alternative contact information through enrichment, and either updates the contact record or routes them to a re-engagement workflow:

# Create a bounce remediation agent
mailclaw agent create --name "bounce-handler" \
  --trigger "bounce.hard" \
  --actions "enrich,find-alternative,notify-owner"

This agent will fire every time a hard bounce is recorded. It'll first attempt to enrich the contact and discover an alternative email address. If one is found, it updates the record and requeues the contact. If not, it suppresses the address and optionally notifies the account owner through the dashboard.

Pro tip: Configure your bounce agent to also check LinkedIn data during enrichment. Many hard bounces happen because someone changed jobs — and their new work email is often discoverable through professional network data.

Monitoring Deliverability Health in the MailClaw Dashboard

MailClaw's local dashboard at localhost:3100 gives you a real-time view of your deliverability health. The Deliverability Monitor panel tracks:

  • Hard and soft bounce rates per campaign and per sending account
  • Spam complaint rates (critical for Gmail and Outlook delivery)
  • Suppression list growth over time
  • Domain and IP reputation indicators from integrated sources
  • Per-sequence bounce breakdowns so you can spot problematic list segments

When your bounce rate on a specific sequence climbs above a configurable threshold, MailClaw will automatically pause that sequence and surface an alert — preventing a bad list segment from damaging your overall sender reputation.

Setting Deliverability Alerts

# Set a bounce rate threshold alert for a specific campaign
mailclaw campaign set-alert --campaign "q4-outreach" \
  --metric bounce_rate \
  --threshold 0.03 \
  --action pause_and_notify

Best Practices for Keeping Your Lists Clean Long-Term

Bounce management isn't a one-time task — it's an ongoing practice. Here are the habits that separate high-deliverability senders from everyone else:

  1. Never import unverified lists. If you're adding contacts from a trade show scan, a purchased list, or a CSV export from an old CRM, run them through MailClaw's enrichment and validation pipeline first. Every time.
  2. Set up a sunset policy. Contacts who haven't opened or clicked in 6–12 months should be moved to a re-engagement sequence or suppressed. Unengaged contacts that eventually bounce are doubly damaging.
  3. Use double opt-in for inbound signups. If you're capturing leads through a form, double opt-in confirms the address is real and actively monitored before it ever enters your sequences.
  4. Monitor sending account health separately. MailClaw's multi-account support means you can spread sends across multiple accounts. Keep a close eye on each account's bounce rate independently — a single bad list segment can tank one account while leaving others healthy.
  5. Review your suppression list quarterly. Hard-bounced addresses should stay suppressed. But soft-bounced addresses that were paused might be worth retesting after 90 days — sometimes mailboxes get cleaned up and become active again.

A Clean List Is a High-Converting List

Bounce management often feels like maintenance work — unsexy, easy to defer. But the senders who treat deliverability as a core discipline consistently outperform those who treat it as an afterthought. With MailClaw's automated bounce handling, AI agents, contact enrichment pipeline, and real-time deliverability dashboard, you have everything you need to run clean, high-performing campaigns entirely from your local machine.

The infrastructure is open-source, runs on OpenClaw, and lives at localhost:3100 — fully under your control. No black-box SaaS platforms deciding what you can see or what gets automated. Just clean data, smart automation, and emails that actually land.

articles.title: MailClaw for Founders: A Guide to AI-Powered Email Outreach
articles.author: Mike Chen
articles.summary: A practical guide for founders on using MailClaw's AI-powered email agents, sequence builder, and contact enrichment tools to run high-converting outreach campaigns entirely from your local machine.
articles.content:
Why Email Outreach Still Wins — And Why Most Founders Get It Wrong

Cold email is one of the highest-ROI channels available to early-stage founders. No ad spend. No algorithm dependency. Just a well-crafted message landing directly in someone's inbox. The problem isn't the channel — it's the execution. Most founders send the same generic pitch to 500 people, wonder why they get a 1% reply rate, and conclude that cold email "doesn't work."

It works. You're just not doing it right yet.

MailClaw was built to fix exactly this. As an open-source, AI-powered email automation tool that runs entirely on your local machine at localhost:3100, it puts enterprise-grade outreach infrastructure in the hands of founders who don't have a sales team, a marketing budget, or six hours a day to manually follow up with leads. This guide walks you through how to use it — practically and effectively.

Getting Started: Your Local Outreach Stack

One of MailClaw's biggest advantages is that it runs locally. There's no SaaS subscription, no data leaving your machine to a third-party server, and no vendor lock-in. It's built on OpenClaw, the underlying AI orchestration engine, which means the agent logic is transparent, forkable, and extensible.

Once you've installed MailClaw, spin up the dashboard with:

mailclaw start

Your local dashboard is now live at http://localhost:3100. From here you can manage every aspect of your outreach: connect email accounts, build sequences, review contact enrichment data, monitor deliverability, and watch your AI agents work in real time.

Connecting Your Email Accounts

MailClaw supports both SMTP and OAuth authentication. For most founders, the fastest path is OAuth with Gmail or Outlook:

mailclaw accounts add --provider gmail --oauth
mailclaw accounts add --provider outlook --oauth

If you're running outreach at scale or using a dedicated sending domain, you can plug in SendGrid, Mailgun, or any custom SMTP configuration:

mailclaw accounts add \
  --provider smtp \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --user apikey \
  --pass YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY

MailClaw supports multi-account sending out of the box, so you can rotate across multiple inboxes to protect deliverability and scale volume without hammering a single domain's reputation.

Contact Enrichment: Know Who You're Emailing Before You Hit Send

Generic outreach fails because it treats a VP of Engineering at a Series B fintech the same as a solo developer at a two-person startup. They are not the same. They don't have the same problems, budgets, or decision-making timelines.

MailClaw's contact enrichment layer fills in the gaps before your sequences ever run. Drop in a list of company domains or LinkedIn URLs and let the enrichment agent do the research:

mailclaw enrich --input leads.csv --output enriched_leads.csv

The enrichment pipeline pulls in data like company size, funding stage, tech stack signals, job titles, and recent news mentions — the kinds of details that make personalization feel genuine rather than templated. If you're already using HubSpot or Salesforce as your CRM, you can sync enriched contacts directly:

mailclaw sync --crm hubspot --file enriched_leads.csv
mailclaw sync --crm salesforce --file enriched_leads.csv

This keeps your pipeline clean and ensures follow-up tasks get created in the right place without manual data entry.

Building Your First AI-Powered Sequence

The sequence builder is where MailClaw starts to feel genuinely different from tools like Lemlist or Instantly. Instead of writing every email yourself and hoping the merge tags don't look robotic, you define the intent of each step and let the AI agent draft contextually relevant copy for each contact based on their enrichment data.

Defining a Sequence

Create a new sequence from the CLI or the dashboard:

mailclaw sequence create --name "founder-outreach-q3"

Then add steps. A solid cold outreach sequence for founders typically follows this structure:

  1. Day 0 — The Cold Open: Short, specific, no-pitch. Reference something real about their company or role.
  2. Day 3 — The Value Add: Share a relevant insight, resource, or case study. No ask yet.
  3. Day 7 — The Soft Ask: Light call to action — a 15-minute call, a quick question, a demo offer.
  4. Day 14 — The Breakup: A final, brief message that closes the loop and invites a reply if timing is off.

In MailClaw's sequence builder, each step accepts a prompt template that the AI agent uses to generate personalized copy:

mailclaw sequence add-step \
  --sequence "founder-outreach-q3" \
  --day 0 \
  --prompt "Write a 3-sentence cold email to {{contact.first_name}} at {{contact.company}}. 
Reference their recent {{contact.news_mention}}. 
Tone: direct, founder-to-founder, no fluff. No call to action."

The AI agent — powered by the OpenClaw engine under the hood — generates a unique email for each contact at send time, not a single template blasted to everyone. The difference in reply rates is significant.

AI Email Agents: Letting the Automation Actually Think

Beyond sequences, MailClaw lets you deploy AI email agents that can handle responses, qualify leads, and even book meetings without you lifting a finger. This is where things get genuinely powerful for a founder managing outreach solo.

An agent can be configured to:

  • Detect positive replies and draft a follow-up that moves toward booking a call
  • Identify objection patterns ("not the right time," "we already have a solution") and respond with appropriate counter-messaging
  • Flag hot leads for immediate human review in the dashboard
  • Auto-pause sequences when a contact replies with an unsubscribe or opt-out signal

Spin up an agent for your active sequence:

mailclaw agent create \
  --name "reply-handler" \
  --sequence "founder-outreach-q3" \
  --mode auto-reply \
  --escalate-on positive

You stay in control. The dashboard at localhost:3100 surfaces every agent action with full transparency — what it sent, why it sent it, and what the contact's reply contained. You can override, edit, or pause at any time.

Deliverability: The Silent Killer of Outreach Campaigns

You can write the world's best email sequence and still get zero replies if your messages land in spam. Deliverability is the unsexy foundation that everything else depends on.

MailClaw's Built-In Deliverability Tools

MailClaw includes a deliverability monitoring suite that runs continuously in the background:

  • Inbox placement testing — sends test messages to seed accounts across Gmail, Outlook, and others to check where you're landing
  • Domain reputation scoring — monitors SPF, DKIM, and DMARC status for your sending domains
  • Bounce and complaint tracking — automatically suppresses contacts who hard bounce or mark you as spam
  • Send-rate throttling — caps daily volume per account to stay within safe warming thresholds
mailclaw deliverability check --account founders@yourdomain.com

Founder tip: If you're starting with a fresh sending domain, run a 2–3 week warmup before launching any real sequences. MailClaw's warmup mode gradually increases send volume and seeds positive engagement signals automatically. Don't skip this step.

Measuring What Actually Matters

Open rates are a vanity metric, especially post-Apple MPP. Focus your attention on reply rate and positive reply rate. A 15% reply rate with 40% of those being positive is a healthy campaign. A 40% open rate with 0.5% replies means your subject lines work but your emails don't.

MailClaw's dashboard breaks this down by sequence, by step, and by account so you can identify exactly where drop-off is happening and iterate quickly. If step two of your sequence is where everyone goes cold, that's your signal to rewrite the value-add email — not the entire campaign.

The Founder's Edge: Authenticity at Scale

The best thing about MailClaw isn't any single feature. It's that it gives you the infrastructure to be genuinely personal at a scale that would otherwise require a full SDR team. When the AI agent references a prospect's Series A announcement, or acknowledges that their company is hiring aggressively in engineering, that's not a gimmick — it's a signal that you've done your homework.

People buy from people who understand them. MailClaw helps you demonstrate that understanding efficiently, so you can spend your limited founder hours on the conversations that actually move the needle — not on copy-pasting follow-up emails at midnight.

The code is open source. The data stays local. The leverage is yours.

articles.title: How to Build an Email Automation Champion Program with MailClaw
articles.author: Anna Liu
articles.summary: Learn how to design and launch an Email Automation Champion Program using MailClaw — turning one power user into a company-wide force multiplier for smarter outreach, better deliverability, and scalable campaign management.
articles.content:
What Is an Email Automation Champion Program?

Most teams adopt an email automation tool, get a few sequences running, and then plateau. The tool becomes one person's side project instead of a company-wide advantage. An Email Automation Champion Program solves that by designating one or more internal advocates — Champions — who own the strategy, tooling, and training around email automation for the entire organization.

With MailClaw running locally on your Mac at localhost:3100, the barrier to becoming a Champion is unusually low. There's no vendor lock-in, no per-seat pricing headache, and no black-box AI you can't inspect or modify. Everything runs on OpenClaw under the hood, which means your Champion can go as deep as they want — tweaking prompts, building custom agents, or wiring up integrations with tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, or SendGrid.

This guide walks you through building that program from scratch: who the Champion should be, how to structure their responsibilities, and the exact MailClaw workflows they should master first.

Choosing and Onboarding Your First Champion

The Champion Profile

Your Champion doesn't need to be a developer — but they should be curious, detail-oriented, and genuinely interested in how email works. Look for someone who:

  • Already writes most of the team's outreach copy or manages sequences manually
  • Asks questions like "why is our open rate dropping?" rather than just accepting the number
  • Is comfortable working in a terminal or learning to be
  • Has relationships across sales, marketing, and ops — because email automation touches all three

Day One: Getting MailClaw Running

Start by getting MailClaw installed and connected. The onboarding experience is designed to be fast — your Champion should be operational within 20 minutes.

# Clone and install MailClaw
git clone https://github.com/openclaw/mailclaw.git
cd mailclaw
npm install

# Start the local dashboard
npm run start
# Dashboard available at http://localhost:3100

Once the dashboard is live, connect your first sending account. MailClaw supports OAuth for Gmail and Outlook (ideal for low-friction setup) as well as raw SMTP credentials for SendGrid, Mailgun, or any custom mail server. Champions managing multiple brands or territories can add several accounts and switch between them from a single dashboard view.

# Add a Gmail account via OAuth
mailclaw accounts add --provider gmail --label "outreach-primary"

# Or add SendGrid via SMTP
mailclaw accounts add --provider smtp \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --user apikey \
  --pass YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY \
  --label "sendgrid-bulk"

Core Workflows Every Champion Must Master

1. Contact Enrichment at Scale

Raw contact lists are a liability — stale data kills deliverability and wastes sequences on the wrong people. MailClaw's built-in contact enrichment layer, powered by OpenClaw's AI pipeline, can take a CSV of names and domains and return enriched profiles with job titles, company size, LinkedIn signals, and more.

# Enrich a contact list before importing
mailclaw contacts enrich --input raw-leads.csv --output enriched-leads.csv --fields title,company,linkedin

Your Champion should establish a pre-send enrichment checklist: every list gets enriched before it enters a sequence. This isn't just about personalization — it's about segmentation. A VP of Sales at a 500-person SaaS company needs a different message than an SDR at a 10-person agency, even if they're both on your "SaaS leads" list.

2. Building Sequences That Actually Convert

The MailClaw sequence builder is where Champions spend most of their time. Sequences are defined in clean YAML and previewed in the local dashboard — so your Champion can see exactly what each recipient will experience before a single email goes out.

# sequences/saas-outbound.yaml
name: SaaS Outbound - Q3
account: outreach-primary
steps:
  - day: 0
    subject: "Quick question about {{company}}'s onboarding flow"
    template: templates/intro.html
    ai_personalize: true

  - day: 3
    subject: "Following up — thought this might help"
    template: templates/followup-1.html

  - day: 7
    subject: "Last one from me, {{first_name}}"
    template: templates/breakup.html
# Deploy the sequence
mailclaw sequences deploy saas-outbound.yaml

# Preview before sending
mailclaw sequences preview saas-outbound --contact john@example.com

Note the ai_personalize: true flag on step one. When this is enabled, MailClaw's OpenClaw-powered AI agent rewrites the email body for each contact using their enriched profile — inserting relevant references to their industry, company size, or recent signals without you writing dozens of variants manually.

3. Deploying AI Email Agents

This is where MailClaw separates itself from tools like Mailchimp or Instantly. An AI email agent isn't just a sequence with merge tags — it's an autonomous loop that monitors replies, categorizes intent (interested, not now, unsubscribe, referral), and takes follow-up actions accordingly.

# Create a new AI agent
mailclaw agents create \
  --name "SDR Assist" \
  --trigger reply \
  --actions categorize,notify,log-to-crm \
  --crm hubspot

Champions should define at least three agent behaviors in their first month:

  1. Interest detector: Flags replies with buying signals and pings the assigned rep via Slack or email
  2. Out-of-office handler: Detects OOO replies and pauses the sequence until the contact returns
  3. CRM logger: Pushes every meaningful reply event to HubSpot or Salesforce automatically, eliminating manual data entry

4. Deliverability Monitoring — The Hidden Multiplier

Champions who ignore deliverability eventually watch their open rates crater and wonder why. MailClaw's deliverability dashboard (accessible at localhost:3100/deliverability) surfaces the metrics that matter: spam rate by domain, bounce categorization, blacklist status, DKIM/SPF/DMARC pass rates, and sending reputation trends over time.

"The best sequence in the world is worthless if it lands in spam. Deliverability isn't a one-time setup — it's an ongoing discipline."

Set your Champion up with a weekly deliverability review ritual. Every Monday, they should check:

  • Bounce rate per sending account (hard bounces above 2% need immediate action)
  • Spam complaint rate (keep below 0.1% — Google and Yahoo now enforce this)
  • Domain warm-up progress for any new sending domains
  • DMARC report summaries for alignment failures
# Pull a deliverability summary from the CLI
mailclaw deliverability report --account outreach-primary --range 7d

Scaling the Program: From One Champion to a Team

Building a Playbook Library

Once your first Champion has three or four working sequences and a few agents live, the next step is documentation. MailClaw's open-source nature makes this unusually clean — sequences are YAML files, agents are defined in config, and everything lives in version control. Your Champion's job is to turn that into a living playbook: a Git repo of battle-tested sequences, enrichment scripts, agent configs, and annotated notes on what worked and why.

Structure the repo like this:

mailclaw-playbook/
├── sequences/
│   ├── cold-outbound-saas.yaml
│   ├── post-demo-followup.yaml
│   └── re-engagement-6mo.yaml
├── agents/
│   ├── interest-detector.yaml
│   └── ooo-handler.yaml
├── templates/
│   └── intro.html
└── README.md  ← The Champion's notes on when to use each

Training Secondary Champions

A program with a single Champion is a single point of failure. Once the playbook exists, run a monthly 60-minute internal workshop where the primary Champion walks colleagues through one new sequence or agent. Keep it practical — live demos in the localhost:3100 dashboard, not slide decks.

Secondary Champions don't need to master the CLI. MailClaw's local dashboard is designed to be approachable for non-technical users: they can clone a sequence, swap out templates, adjust timing, and launch a campaign entirely from the UI. The CLI is for power users; the dashboard is for everyone else.

Connecting the Ecosystem

As the program matures, your Champions should be the people who own the integrations between MailClaw and the rest of your stack. Common high-value connections include:

  • HubSpot or Salesforce: Sync contact enrichment data back to your CRM so sales reps see the same signals MailClaw acted on
  • SendGrid: Route high-volume broadcast campaigns through SendGrid while keeping personalized outreach on Gmail or Outlook
  • Slack: Use agent webhooks to post real-time reply alerts to a #hot-leads channel
  • Google Sheets: Let non-technical teammates submit new contact batches via a form that feeds directly into MailClaw's enrichment pipeline

Measuring Champion Program Success

Define success metrics before you start, or you'll be measuring vanity. The right metrics for a Champion program are:

  • Sequence coverage: What percentage of outreach is now automated vs. manual?
  • Reply rate trend: Are AI-personalized sequences outperforming the old templates?
  • Time saved: How many hours per week has the team reclaimed from manual follow-up?
  • Deliverability score: Is sending reputation stable or improving quarter-over-quarter?
  • Agent actions fired: How many CRM entries, Slack alerts, or paused sequences did agents handle automatically?

MailClaw's dashboard exports these as CSV or JSON for easy reporting. Champions should share a monthly one-pager with leadership — not to justify the tool's existence, but to surface opportunities: sequences that should be retired, segments that need new messaging, or integrations worth building next.

The teams that win at email automation aren't the ones with the most complex sequences. They're the ones with a dedicated human who cares enough to keep the system honest, current, and continuously improving. That's what the Champion program is really about — and MailClaw gives them exactly the right toolkit to do it.

articles.title: Reducing Email Fatigue with MailClaw Smart Throttling
articles.author: David Torres
articles.summary: Learn how MailClaw's smart throttling system prevents email fatigue, protects sender reputation, and keeps your outreach campaigns landing in the inbox — with practical configuration tips and real-world examples.
articles.content:
Why Email Fatigue Is Silently Killing Your Campaigns

You've spent hours crafting the perfect sequence. Your subject lines are sharp, your copy is tight, and your offer is genuinely compelling. But open rates keep sliding, replies dry up after the first touch, and your deliverability dashboard is flashing amber. The culprit? Email fatigue — and it's more nuanced than simply sending too many messages.

Email fatigue happens at two levels. There's recipient fatigue, where contacts stop engaging because they feel overwhelmed or spammed. And there's sender fatigue, where your sending infrastructure — your IP reputation, domain health, and ESP trust score — degrades because you're pushing volume too aggressively. Both are devastating, and both are largely preventable with smart throttling.

MailClaw's built-in throttling engine, powered by the OpenClaw runtime, addresses both problems simultaneously. Instead of leaving pacing decisions to guesswork or a single global "sends per hour" slider, it applies dynamic, context-aware controls at the contact, sequence, and account level — all managed from your local dashboard at localhost:3100.

Understanding the Three Layers of MailClaw Throttling

Before diving into configuration, it helps to understand how MailClaw thinks about send volume. The system operates on three distinct layers, each with its own controls.

1. Account-Level Rate Limits

Every connected sending account — whether that's a Gmail workspace via OAuth, an Outlook tenant, or a transactional provider like SendGrid or Postmark — has its own throughput ceiling. MailClaw respects these upstream limits automatically and lets you set conservative soft caps below the hard limits to protect your reputation headroom.

In your mailclaw.config.json, account-level throttling looks like this:

{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "id": "outreach-gmail",
      "provider": "gmail",
      "auth": "oauth",
      "throttle": {
        "maxPerHour": 80,
        "maxPerDay": 400,
        "minIntervalSeconds": 45,
        "warmupEnabled": true,
        "warmupDays": 14
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "sendgrid-transactional",
      "provider": "sendgrid",
      "auth": "smtp",
      "throttle": {
        "maxPerHour": 500,
        "maxPerDay": 5000,
        "minIntervalSeconds": 7
      }
    }
  ]
}

The warmupEnabled flag is particularly important for new domains or accounts. When active, MailClaw will automatically ramp volume from 10% of your daily cap on day one, increasing by roughly 15% each day until the warmup period completes — mimicking organic growth patterns that ISPs trust.

2. Sequence-Level Pacing

Beyond raw volume, how emails are spaced within a sequence has a huge impact on engagement. A contact who gets three emails in four days will respond very differently than one who receives the same three emails over two weeks with intelligent wait conditions.

In the MailClaw sequence builder, you can set pacing rules directly on each step:

mailclaw sequence create \
  --name "Q3 Prospecting Flow" \
  --step "email:intro" \
  --wait "3d" \
  --step "email:follow-up-1" \
  --wait "5d:no-open" \
  --step "email:follow-up-2" \
  --wait "7d:no-reply" \
  --step "email:breakup" \
  --throttle-per-day 50

The --wait conditions here are doing real work. The no-open flag means the follow-up only sends if the previous email wasn't opened — contacts who did open get a different branch. The --throttle-per-day 50 cap ensures this sequence never floods your sending account even if a large import triggers it simultaneously for thousands of contacts.

3. Contact-Level Frequency Caps

This is where MailClaw really differentiates itself. Using OpenClaw's enrichment pipeline, every contact in your system carries a dynamic engagement score based on historical interaction data — opens, clicks, replies, bounce history, and even timezone signals pulled during contact enrichment.

You can set global contact-level frequency rules that apply across all sequences:

mailclaw contacts set-policy \
  --max-emails-per-week 3 \
  --min-days-between-sequences 14 \
  --suppress-after-bounces 1 \
  --suppress-after-unsubscribes true

This means a contact can never receive more than three emails per week from any of your active sequences, regardless of how many campaigns they're enrolled in. If a HubSpot or Salesforce sync drops the same lead into two overlapping sequences, MailClaw's deduplication and frequency cap layer will silently protect them — and you.

Using AI Email Agents to Adapt Throttling Dynamically

Static throttle rules are a good baseline, but they can't account for real-time signals. That's where MailClaw's AI email agents earn their keep.

You can configure an agent to monitor sequence performance and automatically adjust pacing based on what it observes:

mailclaw agent create \
  --name "Throttle Optimizer" \
  --trigger "sequence:performance-check" \
  --interval "daily" \
  --actions "adjust-pacing,flag-fatigue-risk,pause-underperformers"

Once active, this agent will evaluate open rate trends, reply rates, and unsubscribe velocity for each active sequence every 24 hours. If it detects that open rates on a particular step have dropped more than 20% week-over-week, it will automatically extend the wait before that step by 48 hours and surface a notification in your localhost:3100 dashboard.

Pro tip: Connect your deliverability monitoring feed to the same agent. If your domain's spam placement rate spikes — which you can track natively in the MailClaw deliverability panel — the agent can temporarily drop your send rate across all accounts until the signal recovers.

Practical Throttling Strategies for Common Scenarios

Cold Outreach on a Fresh Domain

If you're launching outreach on a new domain, throttling isn't optional — it's survival. Start with a 14-to-21-day warmup period, cap daily sends at 20 for the first week, and use only your highest-confidence contacts (enriched with verified email addresses) during the warmup window.

  • Enable warmupEnabled: true on the account config
  • Set minIntervalSeconds to at least 90 to avoid burst patterns
  • Use MailClaw's contact enrichment to filter out risky or unverified addresses before warming starts
  • Monitor your spam rate in the deliverability dashboard daily during the first two weeks

High-Volume Sales Sequences to Known Contacts

If you're sending to an opted-in list or warm leads synced from Salesforce, you can run more aggressively — but cadence still matters. The goal is to feel human, not automated.

  • Use randomized send windows: instead of sending at exactly 9:00 AM, configure a 60-minute jitter window so sends are distributed naturally
  • Enable timezone-aware delivery using enriched contact data so each contact receives email during their local business hours
  • Cap any single sequence at no more than 6 touches over 30 days for non-responsive contacts
mailclaw sequence update "Q3 Prospecting Flow" \
  --send-window "09:00-11:00" \
  --send-jitter 60 \
  --timezone-aware true \
  --max-touches 6

Re-Engagement Campaigns to Cold Lists

Re-engagement is high-risk territory. These contacts have already shown they're not excited to hear from you, so throttle aggressively and let engagement signals drive everything.

  1. Segment your cold list by last-engagement date using the MailClaw contact enrichment filters
  2. Start with a single re-engagement email to the smallest, most-recent segment first
  3. Wait 72 hours and check open rates before advancing to the next segment
  4. Use an AI agent to automatically suppress contacts who don't engage after the first touch
  5. Never send more than two emails to a contact who hasn't opened anything in 90+ days without explicit permission reset

Reading the Deliverability Signals That Matter

Throttling without feedback is flying blind. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring panel at localhost:3100/deliverability surfaces the metrics you need to make informed pacing decisions:

  • Spam placement rate: The percentage of your emails landing in spam folders across major providers. Anything above 0.3% is a warning sign.
  • Bounce rate by account: Hard bounces should stay below 2%. A spike usually means a bad list import or a contact enrichment issue.
  • Unsubscribe velocity: If unsubscribes are accelerating over a 48-hour window, a sequence is moving too fast.
  • Reply-to-send ratio: This is the metric most senders ignore. A high reply rate is the single strongest positive signal you can send to ISPs.

Connect these signals back to your throttle configuration and treat them as a feedback loop, not a report card. When the numbers move, your configuration should move with them.

Getting Started in Under Five Minutes

If you're already running MailClaw locally, enabling smart throttling across your accounts takes a single command to apply sensible defaults:

mailclaw throttle apply-defaults \
  --warmup-new-accounts \
  --contact-frequency-cap 3/week \
  --sequence-daily-cap 100 \
  --enable-ai-pacing-agent

This will scaffold the baseline configuration, register the AI pacing agent, and open the throttle overview in your dashboard automatically. From there, you can tune each account and sequence independently as your campaigns evolve.

Email fatigue is one of those problems that compounds quietly until it's a crisis. A domain that takes months to warm up can be damaged in a single aggressive send week. The contacts you burn through reckless pacing are ones you can never recover. MailClaw's throttling system exists precisely because sustainable outreach beats maximum outreach — every time.

articles.title: How to Use MailClaw for Personalized Email at Scale Without Being Spammy
articles.author: Ahmad Saroya
articles.summary: Learn how to use MailClaw's AI email agents, contact enrichment, and sequence builder to send genuinely personalized outreach at scale — without triggering spam filters or burning your sender reputation.
articles.content:
The Personalization Paradox in Email Outreach

Every marketer and sales professional faces the same tension: you need to reach hundreds or thousands of people, but the moment your emails feel automated, recipients disengage — or worse, mark you as spam. The solution isn't to send fewer emails. It's to send smarter ones.

MailClaw was built with this exact problem in mind. Running locally on your Mac at localhost:3100, it combines the power of AI-driven personalization with serious deliverability controls so your outreach feels one-to-one even when it's one-to-thousands. Here's how to use it properly.

Start With Contact Enrichment Before You Write a Single Word

Personalization lives and dies on data quality. If all you know about a contact is their email address, your "personalized" email is just a mail merge — and recipients can feel it instantly.

MailClaw's built-in contact enrichment pipeline pulls in contextual signals before your sequences even run. From the dashboard, navigate to Contacts → Enrich and point it at your list. Under the hood, MailClaw uses OpenClaw's data resolution layer to append:

  • Job title and company role
  • Recent LinkedIn activity or published content
  • Tech stack signals (useful for SaaS outreach)
  • Company size, funding stage, and industry vertical
  • CRM data synced from HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive

You can also kick off enrichment directly from the CLI:

mailclaw contacts enrich --input ./leads.csv --output ./enriched.csv --fields title,company,linkedin,techstack

Once your contacts are enriched, you have the raw material for genuine personalization — not just {{first_name}} tokens, but context-aware messaging that actually resonates.

Building Sequences That Don't Feel Like Sequences

The Anatomy of a Good Outreach Sequence

Most spray-and-pray sequences fail for the same reasons: generic openers, identical follow-ups, and zero adaptation based on behavior. MailClaw's sequence builder lets you construct multi-step campaigns with conditional branching so the path adapts to what each recipient actually does.

A well-structured cold outreach sequence in MailClaw typically looks like this:

  1. Email 1 (Day 0): A short, specific opener referencing something real about the contact
  2. Email 2 (Day 3, if no reply): A different angle — add value, don't just follow up
  3. Email 3 (Day 7, if opened but no reply): Soft CTA with social proof
  4. Email 4 (Day 12, if no open): Re-engagement subject line, minimal copy
  5. Breakup email (Day 18): Low-pressure close that often generates responses

In the sequence builder, set conditions at each step using the visual editor or YAML config:

sequence:
  name: saas-cold-outreach-q3
  steps:
    - day: 0
      template: opener_personalized
      condition: always
    - day: 3
      template: value_add_followup
      condition: no_reply
    - day: 7
      template: social_proof
      condition: opened_no_reply
    - day: 12
      template: reengagement
      condition: no_open
    - day: 18
      template: breakup
      condition: no_reply

Using AI Email Agents to Write the Actual Copy

This is where MailClaw genuinely separates itself from tools like Mailchimp, Lemlist, or Instantly. Rather than writing one template and token-substituting names, MailClaw's AI email agents — powered by OpenClaw — generate a unique version of each email per contact using the enriched data you collected.

Activate an AI agent for a sequence step from the dashboard under Sequences → Step → AI Agent, or via CLI:

mailclaw agent create --name "SaaS Opener Agent" \
  --prompt "Write a 3-sentence cold email opener for {{contact.name}} at {{contact.company}}. Reference their recent work in {{contact.industry}} and connect it to how we help {{contact.persona}} teams reduce churn. Keep it conversational, no buzzwords." \
  --model gpt-4o \
  --sequence saas-cold-outreach-q3 \
  --step 0

The agent runs locally through MailClaw's OpenClaw integration, so your contact data never leaves your machine. Each generated email is stored in the sequence draft queue at localhost:3100/sequences/drafts for your review before anything sends.

Pro tip: Always review AI-generated drafts in batch before launching. MailClaw's draft review interface lets you scroll through 50+ emails quickly, flag outliers, and regenerate individual ones. Ten minutes of review can save you from an embarrassing send.

Deliverability Is a Feature, Not an Afterthought

Setting Up Your Sending Infrastructure

Personalized copy means nothing if your emails land in spam. MailClaw includes a deliverability monitoring suite that most standalone outreach tools charge extra for.

Before launching any sequence, connect your sending accounts through Settings → Accounts. MailClaw supports:

  • Gmail and Google Workspace via OAuth 2.0 (no password storage)
  • Outlook and Microsoft 365 via OAuth
  • Custom SMTP for SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, or your own server
  • Multi-account rotation to distribute volume across sending domains

For serious outreach volume, set up a dedicated sending domain (not your primary business domain) and configure it through MailClaw's domain setup wizard:

mailclaw domain setup --domain outreach.yourcompany.com --provider sendgrid --warmup true

The --warmup true flag activates MailClaw's automated warmup scheduler, which gradually ramps sending volume over 2–4 weeks using real engagement signals.

Reading Your Deliverability Dashboard

Navigate to localhost:3100/deliverability to see a live health panel for each connected account. Key metrics to watch:

  • Spam placement rate: Should stay below 0.1% for Gmail, 0.3% for others
  • Bounce rate: Keep hard bounces under 2% — MailClaw auto-suppresses hard bounces
  • Reply rate: A strong signal to inbox providers that your mail is wanted
  • Unsubscribe rate: Spikes here mean your targeting or messaging needs revisiting

MailClaw will surface warnings directly in the dashboard if any metric drifts into danger zones, and it can automatically pause sequences until you review.

The Rules of Non-Spammy Personalization at Scale

Beyond the technical setup, there are behavioral principles that separate good outreach from noise. After running MailClaw across dozens of campaigns, these practices make the biggest difference:

1. Relevance Beats Volume, Every Time

A list of 200 tightly-targeted, well-enriched contacts will consistently outperform a list of 2,000 loosely matched ones. Use MailClaw's contact scoring feature to prioritize your best-fit prospects before wasting sequences on poor matches.

2. Make Unsubscribing Effortless

Every sequence in MailClaw includes one-click unsubscribe handling by default. Don't disable it. People who want off your list are not your customers — making it hard to leave just generates spam reports.

3. Time Your Sends Intelligently

MailClaw's AI agents can infer timezone from contact location data and schedule delivery during local business hours. Enable this in sequence settings under Send Time → Smart Scheduling. Emails arriving at 2am feel automated even if the copy is brilliant.

4. Respect Reply Signals Immediately

This is non-negotiable. Configure MailClaw's reply detection so that any response — even an out-of-office — immediately pauses all subsequent steps for that contact:

mailclaw sequence update saas-cold-outreach-q3 --pause-on-reply true --pause-on-ooo true

Nothing burns goodwill faster than a follow-up that arrives hours after someone already replied.

Putting It All Together: A Repeatable Workflow

Here's the end-to-end workflow that works reliably for MailClaw-powered outreach:

  1. Import your target list into MailClaw and run contact enrichment
  2. Score and segment contacts by fit, persona, and intent signals
  3. Build your sequence with conditional branching in the sequence builder
  4. Assign AI email agents to write personalized copy per contact per step
  5. Review drafts in the localhost:3100/sequences/drafts panel
  6. Verify your sending domain health and DKIM/SPF/DMARC configuration
  7. Launch with smart scheduling and reply-detection active
  8. Monitor the deliverability dashboard daily for the first two weeks

Because MailClaw is open source and runs entirely locally, you own the entire stack. Your contact data stays on your machine, your API keys stay private, and you're not paying per-seat fees to a SaaS vendor while your outreach scales. Fork it, extend it, or wire it into your existing toolchain — it's all available on GitHub under the OpenClaw project.

Personalized email at scale isn't a contradiction. It just requires the right architecture — and now you have one.

articles.title: MailClaw Email Automation Playbook for B2B SaaS Companies
articles.author: Sarah Kim
articles.summary: A practical playbook showing B2B SaaS teams how to use MailClaw's AI email agents, sequence builder, and contact enrichment to build high-converting outbound and nurture campaigns — all running locally on your Mac.
articles.content:
Why B2B SaaS Outreach Breaks Down (And How to Fix It)

Most B2B SaaS companies have the same problem: a promising contact list, a handful of half-finished email sequences, and a stack of disconnected tools that never quite talk to each other. Sales reps are copy-pasting templates. Marketing is guessing at open rates. And nobody really knows whether the drip campaign from three months ago is still running.

MailClaw was built for exactly this situation. Because it runs locally on your Mac at localhost:3100 and is powered by the OpenClaw engine, your team gets enterprise-grade email automation without shipping your contact data to a third-party SaaS platform. Everything — your sequences, your enriched contacts, your AI agents — lives on your machine until you choose to send.

This playbook walks through the core workflows that high-performing B2B SaaS teams use to build, automate, and optimize outreach with MailClaw.

Step 1: Get Your Foundation Right — Accounts and Deliverability

Before you write a single email, set up your sending infrastructure properly. Skipping this step is why most outbound campaigns end up in spam.

Connect Your Sending Accounts

MailClaw supports multi-account sending via SMTP or OAuth, so you can connect Gmail, Outlook, or a dedicated sending domain through SendGrid or Postmark in one place. From your local dashboard, navigate to Settings → Accounts and add each account:

# Start MailClaw and open the dashboard
mailclaw start

# Or add an account directly via CLI
mailclaw accounts add \
  --name "SDR Outbound" \
  --type smtp \
  --host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --port 587 \
  --user apikey \
  --pass YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY

For Gmail or Outlook, use the OAuth flow from the dashboard — it handles token refresh automatically so your sequences don't silently fail after 90 days.

Run a Deliverability Check Before Launch

MailClaw's built-in deliverability tools let you audit your DNS setup, check your sending reputation, and preview how your emails render before a single real send. Run a pre-flight check on any sequence:

mailclaw deliverability check --sequence "q4-saas-outbound"

This surfaces SPF, DKIM, and DMARC issues, flags spam-trigger words in your copy, and estimates inbox placement across major clients. Fix these issues first — a 5-minute audit here saves weeks of wondering why replies dried up.

Step 2: Enrich Your Contacts Before You Write a Word

Generic outreach fails because it's generic. The fix isn't better copywriting — it's better data. MailClaw's contact enrichment pulls in firmographic and technographic context so your emails can reference things that actually matter to the prospect.

Import and Enrich a Contact List

Start with a CSV export from your CRM — HubSpot, Salesforce, or even a raw LinkedIn export works fine. Import it and run enrichment in one command:

mailclaw contacts import --file prospects.csv
mailclaw contacts enrich --list "q4-prospects" --fields company,title,tech_stack,funding

MailClaw appends enriched fields directly to each contact record. Your sequence variables can then reference {{contact.tech_stack}} or {{contact.funding_stage}} to personalize at scale without manual research.

Sync Enriched Data Back to Your CRM

If your team lives in HubSpot or Salesforce, push enriched contacts back after the run:

mailclaw contacts sync --crm hubspot --list "q4-prospects" --direction push

This keeps your CRM as the source of truth while letting MailClaw handle the outreach layer. No duplicate records, no data drift.

Step 3: Build Sequences That Actually Convert

The MailClaw sequence builder lets you design multi-step email workflows with branching logic, wait conditions, and reply detection — all from your local dashboard or via YAML config files that you can version-control alongside your product code.

Anatomy of a High-Converting SaaS Outbound Sequence

A proven structure for cold outbound to mid-market SaaS buyers looks like this:

  1. Day 1 — The Trigger Email: One problem, one insight, one ask. Under 100 words. No attachments.
  2. Day 3 — The Value Add: A relevant case study, benchmark, or resource. Make it feel like a follow-up thought, not a sales pitch.
  3. Day 7 — The Soft Bump: Reply to your own thread. Acknowledge they're busy. Restate the ask in one sentence.
  4. Day 14 — The Permission Close: "Should I close your file, or is this worth a 15-minute call?" This email consistently outperforms everything above it in reply rate.

Define this in MailClaw's sequence builder from the dashboard, or as a YAML file you can share across your team:

sequence:
  name: q4-saas-outbound
  account: SDR Outbound
  steps:
    - day: 0
      subject: "Quick thought on {{contact.company}}'s onboarding flow"
      template: trigger-email.html
    - day: 3
      subject: "Re: Quick thought on {{contact.company}}'s onboarding flow"
      template: value-add.html
      skip_if: replied
    - day: 7
      subject: ""
      thread: true
      template: soft-bump.html
      skip_if: replied
    - day: 14
      subject: ""
      thread: true
      template: permission-close.html
      skip_if: replied

The skip_if: replied flag is critical — it stops the sequence automatically when a prospect responds, so you're never sending a follow-up to someone already in a sales conversation.

Step 4: Deploy AI Email Agents for Ongoing Personalization

This is where MailClaw pulls ahead of traditional tools. AI email agents — powered by OpenClaw — can draft, personalize, and even respond to emails autonomously based on rules you define. Think of them as always-on SDRs that never forget to follow up.

Setting Up Your First AI Agent

From the dashboard under Agents → New Agent, configure an agent to handle a specific workflow. A common setup for B2B SaaS:

mailclaw agent create \
  --name "Inbound Trial Follow-up" \
  --trigger "contact.tag = trial_started" \
  --goal "Book a discovery call within 7 days" \
  --tone professional \
  --max-emails 4 \
  --account "success@yourapp.com"

The agent drafts each email, pulls context from enriched contact fields, and queues them for your review before sending — or you can set it to fully autonomous mode once you trust the output. All drafts are visible in your local dashboard at localhost:3100/agents.

Use Agents for Nurture, Not Just Outbound

AI agents shine in longer nurture workflows where timing and context matter more than volume. Configure an agent to monitor engagement signals — email opens, link clicks, CRM stage changes synced from HubSpot — and trigger personalized touchpoints when a lead re-engages after going cold.

The best AI agent workflows feel like a thoughtful human remembered to follow up at exactly the right moment. That's the bar to aim for — not automation for its own sake.

Step 5: Monitor, Iterate, and Scale

MailClaw's local dashboard gives you a real-time view of every sequence: open rates, click rates, reply rates, bounce rates, and unsubscribes — broken down by account, sequence, and individual step. No waiting for a third-party platform to sync data overnight.

The Metrics That Actually Matter for B2B SaaS Outreach

  • Reply rate over open rate: Opens are vanity. Replies mean someone read it and cared enough to respond — even to say no.
  • Step-level drop-off: If step 2 has a dramatically lower open rate than step 1, your subject line on the follow-up is killing the thread. Fix the subject before changing the copy.
  • Bounce rate by account: A bounce rate above 3% on any sending account will hurt your domain reputation. MailClaw flags this automatically in the deliverability panel.
  • Sequence-to-meeting rate: Track this end-to-end by tagging contacts who booked calls and tracing them back to their originating sequence.

A/B Test at the Sequence Level

MailClaw's sequence builder supports split testing natively. Define two variants and MailClaw distributes sends evenly, then surfaces the winner based on your chosen metric:

mailclaw sequence split-test \
  --sequence-a "q4-saas-outbound-v1" \
  --sequence-b "q4-saas-outbound-v2" \
  --split 50/50 \
  --winner-metric reply_rate \
  --auto-promote after:200sends

Putting It All Together

The B2B SaaS companies that consistently win at outreach aren't necessarily sending more emails — they're sending smarter ones, at better times, to better-understood prospects. MailClaw's combination of local AI agents, contact enrichment, a flexible sequence builder, and honest deliverability tooling gives your team the leverage to do exactly that.

Because it's open source and runs entirely on your machine, you're not locked into a pricing tier or a vendor's roadmap. Your sequences, your agent configs, and your contact data are yours — version-controlled, portable, and auditable.

Start by connecting one account, importing one list, and running one sequence. Measure it. Improve it. Then scale what works. That loop, run consistently, is what separates teams that build pipeline from teams that wonder why outreach isn't working.

Ready to start? Run mailclaw start and open your dashboard at localhost:3100.

articles.title: How to Set Up MailClaw for GDPR and CAN-SPAM Compliance
articles.author: James Rodriguez
articles.summary: Learn how to configure MailClaw for full GDPR and CAN-SPAM compliance, including consent tracking, unsubscribe automation, contact data handling, and audit-ready campaign settings — all from your local dashboard.
articles.content:
Why Compliance Matters Before You Send a Single Email

Email compliance isn't a checkbox you tick after your first campaign goes out — it's infrastructure. The consequences of getting it wrong range from spam folder placement to five-figure fines under GDPR (up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover) and FTC enforcement actions under CAN-SPAM.
