The good news is that MailClaw, running locally on your Mac via localhost:3100, gives you direct control over every layer of your outreach stack. There's no middleware hiding your data, no SaaS vendor making compliance decisions for you.

This guide walks you through configuring MailClaw for both GDPR (EU) and CAN-SPAM (US) compliance — covering consent management, unsubscribe automation, contact data handling, and audit logging. Whether you're sending cold outreach, nurture sequences, or transactional emails through Gmail, Outlook, or SendGrid, these steps will keep your campaigns legal and your sender reputation intact.

Understanding the Core Requirements

GDPR Essentials for Email Senders

GDPR applies whenever you're processing personal data belonging to EU residents, regardless of where your business is based. For email marketers, this means:

  • Lawful basis for processing: You need either explicit consent, legitimate interest (with a documented balancing test), or a contract basis before emailing anyone.
  • Right to erasure: Contacts can request deletion of their data at any time, and you must honor this within 30 days.
  • Data minimization: Only collect and store contact fields you actually need.
  • Transparent identification: Every email must clearly identify who is sending it.
  • Easy opt-out: Unsubscribes must be honored promptly — within days, not a monthly batch process.

CAN-SPAM Requirements at a Glance

CAN-SPAM is less restrictive than GDPR but still carries real teeth. Key requirements include:

  • No deceptive subject lines or sender information
  • A physical postal address in every commercial email
  • A clear and functional unsubscribe mechanism
  • Opt-out requests honored within 10 business days
  • No sending after someone has opted out

CAN-SPAM technically permits cold email as long as you follow the rules. GDPR is stricter — legitimate interest for cold outreach is possible but requires documentation. Know which law governs each contact segment in your list.

Step 1: Configure Sender Identity Correctly

Open your MailClaw dashboard at localhost:3100 and navigate to Settings → Sending Accounts. MailClaw supports SMTP credentials and OAuth authentication for Gmail and Outlook, as well as API-based sending through SendGrid and similar providers.

For each sending account, ensure the following are set accurately:

  1. From Name: Use your real name or your company name — never a generic alias designed to obscure identity.
  2. Reply-To Address: Should be a monitored inbox. CAN-SPAM requires that replies reach a real person.
  3. Physical Address: Add your business address in the account settings. MailClaw's sequence builder can inject this automatically into email footers using the {{sender.address}} variable.

You can verify your sending account configuration via the CLI:

mailclaw accounts list
mailclaw accounts verify --account=hello@yourcompany.com

This checks SMTP connectivity, DKIM signing status, and SPF alignment — all critical for deliverability and sender authentication.

Step 2: Set Up Consent Tracking for GDPR Contacts

MailClaw's contact enrichment engine pulls data from a variety of sources, but enrichment alone doesn't establish lawful basis. You need to track how and when consent was obtained for each contact segment.

Navigate to Contacts → Custom Fields and add the following fields to your contact schema:

  • consent_basis — values: explicit_consent, legitimate_interest, contract
  • consent_date — ISO 8601 timestamp of when consent was captured
  • consent_source — e.g., website_form, event_signup, crm_import
  • gdpr_region — boolean or country code to flag EU contacts

If you're importing contacts from HubSpot or Salesforce, MailClaw's native integrations let you map these fields directly at import time:

mailclaw contacts import \
  --source=hubspot \
  --map="hs_legal_basis:consent_basis" \
  --map="hs_consent_date:consent_date" \
  --gdpr-filter=true

The --gdpr-filter flag automatically excludes contacts without a mapped consent basis from EU-targeted sequences.

Step 3: Automate Unsubscribe Handling

This is where MailClaw's automation layer earns its keep. Head to Settings → Compliance → Unsubscribe Rules and configure the following:

List-Unsubscribe Headers

Enable one-click unsubscribe headers for all outgoing email. This is now a requirement for bulk senders on Gmail and Yahoo, and it's good practice regardless. MailClaw injects both the mailto: and https: variants automatically when this setting is enabled.

Unsubscribe Link in Footer

In your sequence builder, every email template should include the {{unsubscribe_link}} variable in the footer block. MailClaw generates a unique, tracked link per recipient that logs the opt-out event with a timestamp and sequence ID.

Suppression List Sync

When a contact unsubscribes, MailClaw immediately adds them to your global suppression list. If you're running multi-account campaigns, suppression is shared across all sending accounts by default. To verify:

mailclaw suppressions list --format=csv | head -20
mailclaw suppressions check --email=contact@example.com

You can also sync your suppression list bidirectionally with SendGrid or your CRM to ensure opt-outs propagate across your entire stack — critical for GDPR compliance where erasure must be system-wide, not just per-tool.

Step 4: Configure Your AI Email Agents for Compliant Outreach

MailClaw's AI email agents, powered by OpenClaw, can draft, personalize, and schedule outreach autonomously. But autonomous doesn't mean unconstrained. Before deploying an agent, configure its compliance guardrails in Agents → Guardrails:

  • Suppress on opt-out: Enabled by default — agents check the suppression list before every send.
  • Honest subject lines: Enable the subject line audit rule, which flags deceptive patterns like fake "Re:" prefixes or misleading urgency claims that violate CAN-SPAM.
  • Max follow-up limit: Set a hard cap on follow-up emails per contact. For cold outreach under legitimate interest, this also supports your GDPR balancing test documentation.
  • EU contact routing: Configure the agent to route contacts flagged as gdpr_region=true through a separate, consent-verified sequence only.
mailclaw agent configure --agent=outreach-bot \
  --suppress-on-optout=true \
  --subject-audit=true \
  --max-followups=3 \
  --eu-routing=gdpr_sequence_id

Step 5: Enable Audit Logging and Data Retention Policies

GDPR requires you to demonstrate compliance, not just claim it. MailClaw's audit log records every send event, opt-out, enrichment action, and agent decision locally — no data leaves your machine unless you've configured an outbound sync.

To enable full audit logging:

mailclaw config set audit.enabled=true
mailclaw config set audit.retention_days=730
mailclaw config set audit.log_enrichment=true

Set retention_days to match your data retention policy. Two years is a reasonable default for most organizations, but check with your legal team. You can export audit logs at any time:

mailclaw audit export \
  --from=2024-01-01 \
  --to=2024-12-31 \
  --format=json \
  --output=./audit-2024.json

This export is your paper trail if a data subject makes a Subject Access Request or if a regulator comes knocking.

Step 6: Monitor Deliverability as a Compliance Signal

High spam complaint rates aren't just a deliverability problem — under GDPR, a pattern of complaints can be evidence that you're emailing people without proper consent. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring dashboard at localhost:3100/deliverability surfaces complaint rates, bounce rates, and spam trap hits in real time.

Set up alerting thresholds so you're notified before problems escalate:

mailclaw deliverability alerts set \
  --complaint-rate=0.08 \
  --bounce-rate=2.0 \
  --notify=slack://your-webhook-url

Google's postmaster tools and Microsoft's SNDS (Smart Network Data Services) are worth integrating for additional signal if you're sending through Gmail or Outlook infrastructure. MailClaw's deliverability panel includes direct links to both.

Building a Compliance-First Email Culture

Compliance isn't a one-time setup — it's an ongoing discipline. A few final practices worth embedding into your workflow:

  • Audit your contact list quarterly. Remove contacts you haven't been able to reach in 12+ months. Stale lists hurt deliverability and increase GDPR risk.
  • Document your legitimate interest assessments. If you're relying on legitimate interest for cold outreach, write down the balancing test and store it alongside your MailClaw audit logs.
  • Test your unsubscribe flow end-to-end. Send yourself a test email from every active sequence and click the unsubscribe link. Verify it lands in your suppression list within minutes.
  • Review AI agent outputs regularly. OpenClaw-powered agents are powerful, but periodically review the emails they're drafting for tone, claims, and compliance edge cases.

Because MailClaw runs entirely on your local machine, you have complete visibility and control over your data pipeline — something no cloud-based email tool can offer by default. That architectural advantage makes genuine, auditable compliance significantly more achievable. Set it up right from the start, and compliance becomes a competitive edge rather than a constraint.

articles.title: Why Every Sales Team Needs an AI Email Agent Like MailClaw
articles.author: Priya Patel
articles.summary: AI email agents are transforming how sales teams do outreach — and MailClaw gives you a fully local, open-source way to build them yourself without paying per-seat SaaS fees or handing your data to third parties.
articles.content:
The Problem With Modern Sales Outreach

Sales teams are drowning in busywork. The average SDR spends over 60% of their day on tasks that aren't actually selling — researching prospects, writing personalized emails, following up, checking deliverability, and updating CRM records. That leaves precious little time for the work that actually moves deals forward: real conversations with real people.

The tools that were supposed to solve this — bulk email platforms, CRM automations, template libraries — mostly just made the problem worse. You end up with sequences that feel robotic, follow-ups that land in spam, and contact lists that are stale before you even hit send.

What sales teams actually need isn't more automation. They need smarter automation — the kind that understands context, adapts to responses, enriches contact data on the fly, and monitors its own deliverability without someone babysitting it. That's exactly what an AI email agent does, and it's exactly what MailClaw is built to deliver.

What Is an AI Email Agent, Really?

An AI email agent isn't just a template with a {{first_name}} merge tag. It's a persistent, goal-oriented system that can:

  • Research a prospect and craft a genuinely personalized opening line
  • Decide when and how to follow up based on engagement signals
  • Adjust tone and messaging based on the recipient's industry or role
  • Pause outreach when a reply is detected and route it to the right human
  • Monitor bounce rates and spam complaints and self-correct

MailClaw's AI agents, powered by the OpenClaw engine running locally on your machine, can do all of this without sending a single byte of your contact data to an external SaaS platform. Everything runs at localhost:3100 — your data stays yours.

"The best sales emails don't look like sales emails. They look like someone actually did their homework." — Every top-performing SDR ever.

Setting Up Your First AI Email Agent in MailClaw

Getting started is intentionally straightforward. Once MailClaw is installed and running, open your local dashboard at http://localhost:3100 and navigate to the Agents tab. But first, let's do it from the CLI so you understand what's happening under the hood.

Step 1: Initialize a New Agent

# Start MailClaw if it's not already running
mailclaw start

# Create a new AI email agent
mailclaw agent create --name "SDR Outbound Agent" \
  --goal "book-meetings" \
  --tone "professional-warm" \
  --max-touches 5

The --goal flag tells OpenClaw what success looks like. Setting it to book-meetings means the agent will optimize its messaging and follow-up cadence specifically toward getting a reply that converts to a calendar hold — not just an open or a click.

Step 2: Connect Your Email Accounts

MailClaw supports both SMTP and OAuth, so you can connect Gmail, Outlook, or any custom sending domain. For Gmail, OAuth is the recommended path:

mailclaw account add --provider gmail \
  --oauth \
  --label "Primary SDR Account"

If you're using SendGrid or another SMTP relay for higher volume:

mailclaw account add --provider sendgrid \
  --smtp-host smtp.sendgrid.net \
  --smtp-port 587 \
  --label "High-Volume Sender"

Multi-account support means you can rotate sending across multiple inboxes to protect deliverability — a feature that most $500/month SaaS tools lock behind enterprise tiers.

Step 3: Enrich Your Contact List

Before your agent sends a single email, feed it a clean, enriched contact list. MailClaw's built-in contact enrichment pulls job titles, company size, tech stack, LinkedIn data, and recent news — all the signals a good SDR would research manually.

# Import contacts from CSV and enrich automatically
mailclaw contacts import ./prospects.csv \
  --enrich \
  --enrich-fields "title,company_size,tech_stack,recent_news"

If you're pulling contacts from HubSpot or Salesforce, MailClaw has native sync commands:

# Sync from Salesforce (requires API credentials in .env)

  --filter "lead_status=New" \

Enriched contacts give the AI agent the raw material it needs to write emails that actually reference something real — a recent funding round, a tech stack change, a job promotion. That specificity is what separates a 3% reply rate from a 14% one.

Building a Sequence That Converts

MailClaw's sequence builder lets you define a multi-touch campaign with branching logic. Each step can be written by the AI agent, written by you, or a mix of both. Here's a five-touch sequence structure that performs well for most B2B outbound:

  1. Day 1 — The Hook: Personalized cold email referencing a specific pain point or trigger event. Short. Ends with a low-friction ask.
  2. Day 3 — The Bump: A one-line reply to the original thread. "Wanted to make sure this didn't get buried."
  3. Day 7 — The Value Drop: Share a relevant case study, stat, or piece of content. No ask.
  4. Day 12 — The Different Angle: Reframe the problem from a different angle. New subject line, new thread.
  5. Day 18 — The Breakup: The classic low-pressure close. "Is this just bad timing, or not a fit at all?"

In the MailClaw dashboard, you can configure this visually or define it in a YAML sequence file:

# sequences/sdr-outbound.yaml
name: "SDR Outbound 5-Touch"
agent: "SDR Outbound Agent"
steps:
  - day: 1
    type: ai-generated
    template: hook
    subject_strategy: question
  - day: 3
    type: ai-generated
    template: bump
    thread: true
  - day: 7
    type: ai-generated
    template: value-drop
    attach_asset: "case-study-q4.pdf"
  - day: 12
    type: ai-generated
    template: reframe
  - day: 18
    type: ai-generated
    template: breakup
# Load and launch the sequence
mailclaw sequence load ./sequences/sdr-outbound.yaml
mailclaw sequence launch "SDR Outbound 5-Touch" \
  --contacts-tag "q1-prospects" \
  --dry-run

Always run with --dry-run first. The dashboard will preview every email the agent plans to send, letting you catch anything that feels off before it hits inboxes.

Deliverability: The Silent Killer of Outbound Campaigns

You can have the best copy in the world and still fail if your emails land in spam. MailClaw's deliverability monitoring runs continuously in the background and surfaces problems before they compound.

What MailClaw Monitors Out of the Box

  • Bounce rate per sender account — alerts you when a domain starts getting soft bounces above threshold
  • Spam complaint tracking — integrates with SendGrid and Postmark feedback loops
  • SPF, DKIM, and DMARC validation — run on demand or scheduled nightly
  • Inbox placement estimation — seeds test inboxes to check Gmail vs. Outlook placement
  • Sending velocity controls — automatically throttles send rate if signals deteriorate
# Run a full deliverability audit on all connected accounts
mailclaw deliverability audit --all-accounts --report

The audit outputs a detailed report to your local dashboard with a health score per account, specific flags, and recommended fixes. If you're seeing high spam placement on Gmail but clean results on Outlook, the agent will automatically shift that contact segment to a different sending account.
